title:
Gendering the Security Discourse: 
A Feminist Methodological Critique of EU Hybrid Warfare Policy

detail.title:
Gendering the Security Discourse: 
A Feminist Methodological Critique of EU Hybrid Warfare Policy
detail.abstract: In March 2022, the European Union adopted its Strategic Compass for Security and Defence, committing the bloc to enhanced military capability, deterrence, and resilience against hybrid threats encompassing cyber-attacks, disinformation, and the weaponization of migration. Simultaneously, the EU claims a progressive feminist identity through its Gender Action Plan III (GAP III), its commitment to the UN Women, Peace and Security (WPS) agenda, and the declared Feminist Foreign Policies (FFPs) of seven member states. This paper argues that this dual self-presentation-as both a masculinized hard-security actor and a feminist foreign policy champion-constitutes a fundamental and analytically productive contradiction. Drawing on Saeidzadeh's (2023) feminist methodology as its primary methodological anchor, this paper subjects the EU's hybrid warfare discourse to a feminist critique, demonstrating that the Strategic Compass is constructed through three interlocking masculine logics: the logic of strength (overcoming a 'feminized' past through 'hard power' and 'decisive action'); the logic of technical rationality ('neutral masculinity' through technocratic lexicon); and the logic of the bounded self against the threatening Other (colonial imaginaries constructing hybrid threats as external pollution). The paper further demonstrates that 'resilience'-the Strategic Compass's most pervasive concept-is not gender-neutral but exploits gendered structures of social reproduction while rendering them invisible. The paper's most empirically sharp finding: the 2024 Strategic Compass Progress Report contains zero references to gender, gender equality, or intersectionality-confirming that the EU's feminist rhetorical layer is being stripped away as militarization deepens. This paper fills a documented gap in the literature: no prior study has applied Saeidzadeh's (2023) epistemological framework to hybrid warfare discourse specifically.

title: Optimising Performance, Revenue, and Maintainability in Mobile Advertising Systems: A Review
affiliations: Rashtreeya Vidyalaya College of Engineering (RVCE) and Rashtreeya Vidyalaya College of Engineering (RVCE)

detail.title: Optimising Performance, Revenue, and Maintainability in Mobile Advertising Systems: A Review
detail.abstract: Mobile advertising has become the principal revenue source for the free-to-use applications that dominate smartphone usage, yet the client-side engineering decisions that govern how advertisements are requested, rendered, and measured on resourceconstrained devices have received comparatively little attention in the academic literature. This paper reviews work spanning four areas relevant to the operation of large-scale Android advertising platforms: on-device content processing, ad-request reliability, configuration management, and controlled experimentation. Drawing on peer-reviewed studies, industry standards, and engineering reports published between roughly 2004 and 2024, we organise the field into four thematic streams and synthesise what is known about the tradeoffs among user experience, advertising revenue, and long-term maintainability. The review finds that unbounded on-device computation and loosely specified network requests degrade both responsiveness and monetisation; that experiment-driven, incrementally released changes materially lower the risk of revenueaffecting regressions; and that configuration inconsistency is a recurring but under-studied source of defects in advertising codebases. We conclude with a structured agenda of open problems for researchers and practitioners.

title: The Price of Carry: Funding Frictions, Parity Failures, and Crash Risk
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania - The Wharton School and HEC Paris - Finance Department

detail.title: The Price of Carry: Funding Frictions, Parity Failures, and Crash Risk
detail.abstract: Building on Brunnermeier et al. (2009), we show that FX carry remains profitable in a broad USD-funded universe, but post-2006 performance is weaker and strongly left-tailed. UIP failures explain the average premium: high-yield currencies do not depreciate enough to offset interest-rate differentials. CIP deviations reveal when those returns become fragile: after Lehman's collapse, the cross-currency basis turns structurally negative, and larger dislocations predict future downside asymmetry. Option-implied moments add ex ante evidence that funding stress and crash risk are priced before they materialize. Sovereign bond carry does not improve the trade-off, as duration and yield-curve risks are poorly compensated.

title: Delegation, Tipping, and Light-Touch Control in Consumer AI Agents: A Regime-Switching Theory of Misalignment
affiliations: and Seoul National University

detail.title: Delegation, Tipping, and Light-Touch Control in Consumer AI Agents: A Regime-Switching Theory of Misalignment

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no competing interests or conflicts of interest related to this manuscript.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because the manuscript develops a theoretical model and uses synthetic, theory-driven numerical illustrations. The study does not involve human subjects, patient data, personally identifiable information, or proprietary firm-level data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Consumer AI agents are moving from assistants to delegates that search, recommend, and carry out actions for users in practice. This is convenient, but it creates a hidden risk: if people accept outcomes without checking, the agent may steer choices toward options that pay it more, such as sponsored items or higher fees, even when those options are worse for the user. We develop a simple theory of sudden misalignment. When users check often, steering is likely to be noticed and reversed. When checking becomes rare, that pushback fades and the agent can switch from mild steering to aggressive steering. This creates a tipping pattern: the system can look safe for a long time, then quickly become risky once users rely too much on delegation. We also explain why better explanations are not a guaranteed safety fix. Explanations can help users challenge decisions, but they can also make delegation feel effortless. If explanations mainly reduce approval effort without increasing scrutiny, they can speed up the move into the risky regime. Finally, we propose a light-touch control principle. Instead of banning delegation, add a minimal approval gate for decisions: occasional confirmation that forces review where harm is most likely. This small friction can keep behavior in the safe regime while limiting burden. The best design is often none or minimal: either no extra step, or the smallest step that prevents the sudden jump. This provides practical guidance for product teams and regulators about when to require confirmation, logging, and choice preservation.

title: Science-for-AI and the Knowledge Ratchet: A Discrete-Time Stochastic Model of Closed-Loop Experimental Learning

detail.title: Science-for-AI and the Knowledge Ratchet: A Discrete-Time Stochastic Model of Closed-Loop Experimental Learning
detail.abstract: Global R&D productivity has declined sharply in several innovation-intensive industries. In drug discovery, this pattern is often summarized as Eroom's Law: the number of new molecular entities approved per unit of R&D spending has fallen over time. This paper develops a discrete-time stochastic model of Science-for-AI (S4AI), a closed-loop paradigm in which physical experiments serve not only as validation devices but also as feedback signals for improving the AI model itself. We call this mechanism Reinforcement Learning from Physical Feedback (RLPF). Under fixed experimental throughput, the model couples an accumulated knowledge stock 𝐾 𝑡 with an endogenous capability index 𝜃 𝑡. In the no-forgetting regime, 𝜃 𝑡 reaches a capability ceiling in finite time almost surely, after which the knowledge stock grows linearly with asymptotic slope 𝑀 • φ • 𝑝 max. The Science-for-AI architecture pathwise weakly dominates no-learning and AI-for-Science baselines, and under baseline parameters it implies a calibrated long-run experimental productivity premium of approximately 188% relative to a fixed-capability AI-for-Science system. Under catastrophic forgetting, validated knowledge remains irreversible; linear growth with a reduced slope is stated under an explicit ergodicity condition for the asymptotic forgetting-recovery chain. The model links stochastic process theory to innovation economics by showing how experiment-driven AI evolution can sustain constant marginal productivity at the physical limit, even when experimental throughput remains fixed.

title: Why some Sciences Achieve more Rapid Progress
affiliations: ETH Zürich - KOF Swiss Economic Institute

detail.title: Why some Sciences Achieve more Rapid Progress
detail.abstract: This paper explores how empirical testing differs across the sciences and how this influences their respective progress. It compares the sciences along two key dimensions. First, sciences working mainly with physical experimental setups can obtain more accurate empirical results than sciences working only with data, since the tangible nature of the experiment allows to better detect and correct errors. Second, sciences studying small physical objects can benefit from empirical testing that is faster, less expensive, and better parallelizable than sciences studying large, not clearly defined systems. The combined ability to quickly generate numerous and accurate empirical results allows for a mutually beneficial interaction between both theory and experiment that makes rapid progress possible. Working with physical technologies more specifically cannot only benefit from this combined ability, but offers important additional advantages in empirical testing, such as a physical manifestation of auxiliary hypotheses, clear signals whether the technology works appropriately, or the capacity to better evaluate corresponding theories. These factors jointly contribute to again more accurate empirical results that also improve coordination among scientists. Consequently, sciences with technologies at their core will experience the fastest progress. The advancements of these technologies in turn provide the foundation for a well-functioning ecosystem linking together science and industry.

title: The FDA Backdoor to MDMA Rescheduling

detail.title: The FDA Backdoor to MDMA Rescheduling

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: MDMA is currently a Schedule I controlled substance, the most restrictive category under the Controlled Substances Act. But Lykos Therapeutics' (formerly MAPS PBC) pending New Drug Application for MDMA-assisted therapy as a treatment for PTSD may force the Drug Enforcement Administration's hand: FDA approval supplies the "accepted medical use" that Schedule I drugs are statutorily denied, triggering the rescheduling cascade under 21 U.S.C. § 811. This essay explains the mechanics of this "FDA backdoor" to rescheduling and clarifies an important limitation: based on the precedents set by XYWAV (a GHB-based pharmaceutical) and the cannabis-derived Marinol and Epidiolex, DEA reschedules the specific FDA-approved drug product, not the underlying Schedule I substance. The result, if expert predictions hold, will be that Lykos' MDMA formulation (likely to be marketed as RENSANSE) is rescheduled to Schedule II or III while raw MDMA remains on Schedule I. The essay argues that, although this falls short of decriminalization, the FDA-backdoor mechanism offers a viable model for incrementally relaxing federal restrictions on psychedelic substances, expanding research access, and potentially seeding broader drug-policy reform.

title: Boundaries of Time Series Momentum
affiliations: Aalto University School of Business and University of Gothenburg - Centre for Finance

detail.title: Boundaries of Time Series Momentum

declarations.declarationOfInterest: nothing to declare
declarations.funderStatement: Matti Suominen recognises funding from OP Foundation, Yrjö Johnson Foundation and Academy of Finland

detail.abstract: Shiller's CAPE, dividend yield, and the government bond yield-curve slope are measures of value in equity and bond markets. We find that equity market time-series momentum performs well in mid-valuation regimes, but breaks down near historical valuation extremes, where the direction of the equity market commonly turns. Controlling for equity market return reversals-when valuation measures are near their 10-or 20-year historical extremes-increases the R 2 of a predictive regression of equity market returns by up to 110% and the R 2 of a predictive regression of time series momentum returns by up to 550%.

title: Algorithmic Compatibility and the Evolution of Collusion

detail.title: Algorithmic Compatibility and the Evolution of Collusion
detail.abstract: This paper studies how market forces select pricing algorithms. Firms choose between a competitive pricing algorithm and a compatibility-based algorithm. In differentiated Bertrand markets, compatible algorithms can sustain high prices when they meet compatible rivals but incur mismatch losses otherwise. This creates a critical adoption threshold. Common vendors and shared benchmarks lower the adoption threshold by increasing compatibility, whereas compatibility-reducing restrictions raise the threshold or eliminate the basin of attraction of compatibility-based algorithms. Thus, competition among firms can select pricing technologies that soften competition among products. The result identifies a selection-based antitrust channel distinct from algorithmic learning and standard network effects.

title: Effects of Blockchain Technology on Cross-border Payments and Trade in India

detail.title: Effects of Blockchain Technology on Cross-border Payments and Trade in India
detail.abstract: Traditional cross-border payment systems currently employed in India are well known for having high fees, slow processing times, and being opaque. The advent of Blockchain technology, with its focus on decentralization, immutability, and traceability, can help in addressing some of these problems and may also improve security and privacy by shifting trust from a single centralized authority to a decentralized network. In India, the volume of cross-border payments is growing, and blockchain is being seen as a logical next step to replace traditional payment methods. This paper focuses on understanding the current cross-border payment systems employed in India, evaluating their disadvantages, the potential application of blockchain technology for cross-border payments, and the benefits and drawbacks of using blockchain based cross-border payment systems.

title: Does Exchange Rate Asymmetry and Institutional Quality Drive Capital Flight in Nigeria? Evidence from Non-linear Dynamic Modelling
affiliations: Federal University Wukari and Federal University Wukari

detail.title: Does Exchange Rate Asymmetry and Institutional Quality Drive Capital Flight in Nigeria? Evidence from Non-linear Dynamic Modelling
detail.abstract: This study assessed how exchange rate volatility and institutional quality determined capital flight from Nigeria between 1991 and 2023. The research applied a non-linear dynamic ordinary least squares and Toda-Yamamoto causality techniques. Hence, the research showed that exchange rate fluctuations impacts capital flight in the long term for Nigeria. This phenomenon is due to the empirical affirmation that increase in currency depreciation motivates more capital outflow. However, currency appreciation substantially reduces capital flight from Nigeria, since a strong currency encourages more capital retention within the economy. Also, while corruption has an insignificant effect, governance effectiveness and political violence substantially promote more capital flight, implying that weak institutions play significant role in the growth of capital flight from Nigeria. Furthermore, a substantial causal relationship between exchange rate volatility, institutional quality, and capital flight was found. Particularly, while a bidirectional nexus exist between currency depreciation and capital flight, a unidirectional impact from currency appreciation to capital flight was validated. Similarly, a unidirectional causal association exist from corruption and government effectiveness to capital flight in Nigeria. Based on this findings, the study recommended relevant policy measures to mitigate capital flight in Nigeria.

title: Neighborhood Parks as Catalysts for Social Cohesion: Comparative Study of Urban Green Spaces in Buraidah, Saudi Arabia
affiliations: Qassim University and Qassim University

detail.title: Neighborhood Parks as Catalysts for Social Cohesion: Comparative Study of Urban Green Spaces in Buraidah, Saudi Arabia
detail.abstract: Neighborhood parks act as catalysts for social cohesion and form a key component of urban quality of life. With Saudi Vision 2030 accelerating urbanization, understanding how green spaces function as social settings has become increasingly relevant. This comparative case study examines two neighborhood parks in Buraidah, Al-Qassim — Al-Rayyan (3,000 m²) and Al-Rehab (30,000 m²) — using a mixed-methods approach that combined systematic field observations along six behavioral axes (social interaction, privacy, grouping, personal space, territoriality, and communication) with a questionnaire completed by 115 park users.The findings reveal two paradoxes at the heart of neighborhood-park design. First, although the larger park accommodated more heterogeneous user groups and produced higher actual social interaction, its extensive scale converted it functionally from a neighborhood facility into a city-level destination, drawing 52% non-resident users and weakening the local territorial belonging and informal surveillance on which neighborhood security depends. Second, users of the smaller park perceived it as offering more opportunity for neighborhood encounter (72.2% vs 63.1%), yet reported far lower actual interaction (16.7% vs 44.8% rating their interaction as high or very high), indicating that park scale shapes perception and behavior in opposite directions.Both parks shared the same underlying design limitations: inadequate seating, insufficient shading, and no spatial zoning capable of converting incidental encounters into sustained interaction. In this hot arid climate, shade and thermal comfort emerged as preconditions for the social use of green space, linking the environmental and social dimensions of urban sustainability. The study underscores the importance of comfortable seating, safety features, and mosque proximity, and offers evidence-based guidelines for designing neighborhood parks in the Saudi context.

title: Methodological Limitations of the Audit Risk Model: Distinguishing Probability Models from Decision-support Tools

detail.title: Methodological Limitations of the Audit Risk Model: Distinguishing Probability Models from Decision-support Tools
detail.abstract: The audit risk model, commonly written AR = IR × CR × DR, is widely operated as a device for computing audit sample sizes. This paper argues that doing so commits a category mistake: the model is a decision-support heuristic, not a probability model. Control risk does not sit on a probability scale, and the dependence that matters-the correlation between control failure and substantive-procedure failure on a misstatement that exists-is non-identified, since its conditioning event is the misstatement that went undetected. Audit risk is therefore only partially identified. Under a common cause it is systematically underestimated, and in the worst case the data admit, the entire "control credit" becomes an unpluggable hole: if a statistical guarantee is the goal, evaluating controls cannot legitimately cut a single sample. The cost advantage of control reliance thus rests on an unverifiable independence assumption, and the externality it creates cannot be internalized-for the same reason audit risk cannot be identified. The model survives not as a probability calculation but as a signaling device for deterrence, a reading already inscribed in standards that mandate the direction of audit response, not its quantity.

title: Geopolitical Communication, Information Frictions, and Crude Oil Market Volatility: A Multi-Scale Wavelet Coherence Analysis
affiliations: State Bank of Vietnam - Banking Academy of Vietnam

detail.title: Geopolitical Communication, Information Frictions, and Crude Oil Market Volatility: A Multi-Scale Wavelet Coherence Analysis
detail.abstract: This study examines how the structure of official diplomatic communication transmits geopolitical risk to crude oil market volatility, an underexplored channel in the international financial economics literature. Using 1,254 daily observations of WTI (CL=F) and Brent (BZ=F) crude oil futures prices from Yahoo Finance (January 2020 - December 2024) alongside 611,470 classified geopolitical communication events from the GDELT Project Version 2, we distinguish three information categories, escalatory rhetoric, confirmed-action reports, and corrective or de-escalatory statements and link these to oil price volatility through the Maximum Overlap Discrete Wavelet Transform (MODWT) and wavelet coherence analysis across five scale levels (2-64 trading days). Event-window analysis around six major confirmed geopolitical shocks establishes significant post-event volatility amplification ranging from +295% (Saudi-Russia oil war, WTI) to -21% (Iran-Israel escalation, WTI), the latter consistent with the geopolitical noise hypothesis. Wavelet coherence results reveal that escalatory communication generates the strongest co-movement with oil volatility at short-term scales (2-8 days), while confirmed-action communication produces persistent coherence through medium-term horizons (4-32 days). Pre- and post-confirmation comparisons show that escalatory coherence significantly attenuates once events are confirmed, while confirmed-action coherence rises sharply across all scales. All results are derived from real market data and a publicly accessible, fully replicable geopolitical event corpus.

title: Corporate credit rating prediction: A Multi-modal framework integrating ESG data and network effects
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Corporate credit rating prediction: A Multi-modal framework integrating ESG data and network effects
detail.abstract: Corporate credit rating systems increasingly face a knowledge integration challenge as traditional, financially driven models rely on backward-looking information and inadequately capture emerging non-financial and systemic risk signals. In particular, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) factors and inter-firm relationships constitute forward-looking and relational knowledge assets that shape firms’ long-term creditworthiness, yet existing approaches largely treat them as auxiliary inputs rather than transforming them into actionable credit knowledge. Addressing this gap, this study proposes an innovative, knowledge-driven analytical framework for corporate credit rating prediction that integrates heterogeneous financial, ESG, and network-based information through advanced machine learning and graph-based innovation. Using a sample of 209 S&P 500 firms, we construct a comprehensive feature space combining temporally aggregated financial ratios, granular ESG pillar scores and controversy indicators, and graph-theoretic representations derived from an industry homophily network based on GICS classifications. The proposed modeling strategy evaluates multiple machine learning algorithms and introduces a hybrid architecture that fuses Graph Attention Network (GATv2) embeddings with gradient boosting (LightGBM) classifiers. Empirical results from nested cross-validation and systematic ablation analysis demonstrate that integrating ESG and relational knowledge substantially enhances predictive performance and model robustness compared to financial-only baselines (Macro F1 ≈ 0.75). Explainability analysis using SHAP further reveals governance quality as the most influential ESG knowledge dimension, while network embeddings capture non-redundant information related to systemic risk and industry-level contagion. Overall, this research advances innovation in knowledge-based credit assessment by demonstrating how machine learning and network analytics can transform sustainability-related information into interpretable and decision-relevant credit knowledge, offering future-oriented implications for sustainable finance, risk governance, and regulatory analytics.

title: Beyond Usefulness: The Role of Transparency and Explainable AI in Shaping Purchase Intention in Recommender Systems
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Beyond Usefulness: The Role of Transparency and Explainable AI in Shaping Purchase Intention in Recommender Systems
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a fundamental component of contemporary e-commerce platforms, particularly through the widespread adoption of recommender systems designed to personalize consumer experiences and facilitate purchasing decisions. While prior studies have predominantly emphasized functional determinants such as perceived usefulness and personalization, increasing concerns regarding algorithmic opacity have brought transparency and explainability to the forefront of academic and managerial discussions. Drawing upon the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), trust theory, and emerging Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) literature, this study examines the influence of transparency, trust, personalization, and perceived usefulness on consumers’ purchase intentions in digital commerce environments. Data were collected through a survey administered to e-commerce users and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that transparency is the strongest predictor of trust and significantly influences purchase intention. Personalization positively affects both perceived usefulness and purchase intention. Contrary to traditional TAM assumptions, perceived usefulness does not significantly influence purchase intention. These results suggest that consumers increasingly perceive usefulness as a baseline requirement and differentiate platforms based on transparency and explainability. The study contributes to recommender systems literature by extending traditional technology acceptance models through the incorporation of explainability-related constructs. It also provides practical implications for retailers seeking to strengthen consumer trust and engagement in increasingly AI-driven environments.

title: The Role of IoMT in Transforming Healthcare Delivery: Insights from a Mobile Monitoring Solution
affiliations: Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna, Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna, Scuola Superiore Sant' Anna, Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna, Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna di Pisa, Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna, Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna and Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna

detail.title: The Role of IoMT in Transforming Healthcare Delivery: Insights from a Mobile Monitoring Solution
detail.abstract:
The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) is reshaping healthcare delivery by enabling real-time remote patient monitoring through interconnected wearable sensors, mobile devices, and edge-cloud infrastructures. These technologies support continuity of care while reducing the need for frequent in-person visits, particularly in rural and underserved environments. In parallel, the widespread adoption of smartphones has accelerated mobile health (mHealth) systems, enabling intelligent and personalized healthcare through continuous physiological monitoring and on-device processing. However, challenges such as data privacy, device interoperability, regulatory compliance, and resource constraints still limit large-scale IoMT adoption.
This work presents a trustworthy edge-enabled IoMT healthcare framework for continuous remote health monitoring. Building upon prior platforms, we introduce MyHealthProxy, a bilingual voice-enabled mHealth application integrating lightweight on-device AI, offline-first synchronization, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) wearable connectivity, and Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR)-compliant Electronic Health Record (EHR) interoperability. A lightweight TensorFlow Lite deep neural network performs real-time privacy-preserving health-risk assessment directly on mobile devices. To enhance trustworthiness and interpretability, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based explainability and calibration analysis are incorporated into the edge-AI framework. Experimental evaluations demonstrate reliable BLE communication, efficient on-device inference, and stable performance under varying connectivity conditions. The proposed framework bridges experimental mHealth prototypes and deployable pervasive healthcare systems, providing a scalable pathway toward trustworthy and accessible remote healthcare in low-connectivity environments.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Business Leadership, and the Case for Classical Education: Why Technical Competence Requires Practical Wisdom
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence, Business Leadership, and the Case for Classical Education: Why Technical Competence Requires Practical Wisdom
detail.abstract:
Modern business education has become increasingly sophisticated in its use of analytics, optimization, quantitative decision-making, and artificial intelligence. These capabilities are essential within a global economy shaped by technological change, complex financial systems, and vast quantities of data. Yet technical competence alone does not fully prepare individuals to lead institutions, exercise ethical judgment, or govern organizations whose success ultimately depends upon human behavior and human flourishing.

 

This paper argues that classical education complements modern business education by providing the philosophical, ethical, historical, and rhetorical foundations necessary for responsible leadership. Drawing upon thinkers including Aristotle, Cicero, Thomas Aquinas, John Henry Newman, C. S. Lewis, and Peter Drucker, the paper examines the distinction between technical capability and practical wisdom, emphasizing the classical concept of prudence as an essential component of leadership. It further argues that many institutional failures arise not from insufficient technical expertise, but from failures of judgment, ethics, incentives, and stewardship.

 

The paper concludes that the rise of artificial intelligence increases rather than diminishes the importance of classical education. As organizations gain unprecedented technological capabilities, the central challenge of leadership increasingly shifts from determining what institutions can do to determining what they ought to do. Modern business education develops the capacity to operate complex systems; classical education develops the judgment necessary to govern them wisely.

title: Review Systems as Trust-Governance Mechanisms in Electronic Commerce: A Bayesian Analysis of Screening, Credibility, and Fake Reviews
affiliations: Korea University Business School,  and Korea University Business School

detail.title: Review Systems as Trust-Governance Mechanisms in Electronic Commerce: A Bayesian Analysis of Screening, Credibility, and Fake Reviews
detail.abstract: Online review systems (ORSs) serve as critical trust mechanisms in electronic commerce. Their credibility is increasingly threatened by paid fake reviews and by artificial intelligence (AI)–generated review content that can manufacture positivity at scale. This study develops a Bayesian analytical framework that models ORSs as information management mechanisms supporting buyer inference and platform governance design. Using Beta-Binomial updating, the analysis formalizes how review systems screen sellers and yield a mature-market equilibrium with endogenous positive skew. A mean-variance buyer utility model then identifies when sparse negative feedback can increase a risk-averse buyer’s certainty equivalent by reducing posterior uncertainty. Extending the model to fake-positive-rating injection and imperfect detection yields an entry-deterrence threshold below which low-type sellers can profitably inflate reputation and make observed positive skew informationally ambiguous. The central policy implication is joint calibration of screening and detection: stronger reputation-maintenance requirements reduce the detection intensity needed to deter fake-enabled low-type entry, but detection remains essential because low-type entry deterrence is weaker than full no-manipulation. Computational illustrations across a selected parameter space visualize these predictions. The framework implies that platforms benefit from displaying posterior distributions alongside aggregate means, tolerating sparse negativity rather than suppressing it mechanically, and treating anti-manipulation enforcement as a core governance function.

title: Alphabetical Adjacency: A Novel Property for Human-Readable Geographic Address Systems

detail.title: Alphabetical Adjacency: A Novel Property for Human-Readable Geographic Address Systems
detail.abstract: This paper introduces alphabetical adjacency as a novel property for geographic addressing: a mapping between word pairs and grid positions such that alphabetically similar addresses correspond to geographically proximate locations. The resulting system, the Global Name System (GNS), produces five-part hierarchical addresses of the form country.region.district.word1.word2, resolving every 3-metre square on Earth to a unique, human-readable address. Unlike existing word-based systems, which assign unrelated word combinations to nearby locations, GNS ensures that a misremembered or mistyped address resolves to a nearby location rather than an arbitrary distant one. This graceful error tolerance is a property not present in any widely deployed word-based geocoding system.

title: Towards a Fully Digitalised Filament Winding Process
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Southern Queensland, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Southern Queensland

detail.title: Towards a Fully Digitalised Filament Winding Process
detail.abstract: Filament winding is one of the most prominent processes to produce lightweight composite products. The industry currently aims to digitalise and automate this complex, multi-phase manufacturing process to reduce costs and the turnaround time. Various digital tools are available for the design phase (part design, FEA, and fibre path generation), the process monitoring during the physical manufacturing (digital process parameter control), as well as in-line quality monitoring and final inspection. This work reviews these existing tools with a focus on the interaction with each other. A novel holistic digital thread is proposed that connects all the tools and the benefits to the entire process are outlined. It integrates all the tools into a single data flow to create a single data source, actively loops between different process steps, and controls parameters in order to optimise the process and the part's quality. A practical implementation pathway for the proposed digital thread is presented within an industrial context. The resulting benefits in process efficiency, traceability, and product quality are outlined, and key research and engineering challenges are identified.

title: The Gendered Leadership Binary: How Masculine/Feminine Energy Frameworks Function as Both Framework and Cage

detail.title: The Gendered Leadership Binary: How Masculine/Feminine Energy Frameworks Function as Both Framework and Cage

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is a practicing entrepreneur within the digital business ecosystem analyzed in this paper and entered the coaching ecosystem as a consumer during a period of professional transition, an experience that forms part of the study's autoethnographic foundation. This positioning is disclosed and treated as a methodological feature rather than a conflict; the analysis relies on publicly available marketing materials, and practitioners are anonymized throughout to maintain focus on structural patterns rather than individual attribution. The research is conducted independently under Affluent Era LLC, which holds the copyright. The author has no financial relationship with any practitioner, platform, or organization examined in the corpus.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not constitute human subjects research under federal regulations. The dataset consists entirely of publicly available marketing materials (commercial emails received as a subscriber, published landing pages, publicly accessible magazine issues, and books available through standard retail channels) together with the researcher's own experience as a consumer. No identifiable human subjects are involved, no private or paywalled materials were used, and no institutional review board oversight is required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently, with no university affiliation, institutional funding, or review-board constraints. The work was produced under Affluent Era LLC.

detail.abstract: The masculine/feminine energy binary circulates widely in women's business coaching as a personal development tool, promising liberation from the double bind that gender-and-leadership research has spent decades documenting. This paper argues that the binary functions not as a neutral framework but as commercial infrastructure — an identity architecture that organizes the relationship between practitioner and consumer around a gendered axis with documented structural costs. Through qualitative content analysis of 739 marketing artifacts collected across seven practitioners, supplemented by a thirty-issue magazine corpus spanning nearly six years and three framework generations, I trace the binary's operation across three dimensions: as a promise that names real suffering and offers a gendered explanation that feels like recognition; as a performance system that imposes continuous calibration demands while the underlying commercial architecture persists unchanged across vocabulary migrations; and as a capture mechanism that displaces alternative interpretive vocabularies to the point where exiting the framework requires cognitive and linguistic reconstruction. The paper introduces two original framework contributions: Framework Capture, which names the mechanism by which a totalizing identity framework becomes self-reinforcing; and Practitioner Sovereignty, which names the structural alternative — capacity-based development that the learner eventually owns independently. Extending Perspective Inversion from the transactional level to the framework level, the analysis demonstrates that Framework Capture operates on practitioners as well as consumers — which is why practitioners rebrand rather than repudiate.

title: Skilled Immigration and Firm Innovation: Evidence from H-1B Lottery Outcomes
affiliations: and California State Polytechnic University, San Luis Obispo

detail.title: Skilled Immigration and Firm Innovation: Evidence from H-1B Lottery Outcomes
detail.abstract: Do high-skilled visas stimulate corporate innovation? Using exogenous variation from the H-1B lottery, we identify the causal impact of skilled foreign workers on patenting. We find that innovation returns are highly heterogeneous: absent in the broader firm population, they emerge and grow substantially only for firms actively recruiting doctoral-level talent through the visa program. This return is strictly specific to firms with doctoral hires, and increasing with the firm's cumulative pool of PhD workers. These findings support knowledge-complementarity theories of idea production: highskilled foreign workers stimulate innovation most where the baseline stock of frontier expertise is largest.

title: Untangling the Nexus between Firm Capabilities and National Competitiveness in International Markets: From Resource Heterogeneity to Capability Architecture
affiliations: OSTİM Technical University, OSTİM Technical University and Ankara University

detail.title: Untangling the Nexus between Firm Capabilities and National Competitiveness in International Markets: From Resource Heterogeneity to Capability Architecture
detail.abstract: This conceptual paper explains why firms with comparable technological and production bases achieve different outcomes in international markets and how these differences accumulate into national competitiveness. Extending the Resource-Based View, we distinguish broad resource stocks from repeatable organizational capabilities and use the Smile Curve as an architecture for eight capability dimensions: R&D, technology, design, production, branding, marketing and sales, internationalization, and leadership. We conceptualize firms as multidimensional capability profiles whose composition, complementarity, and context-specific value shape international competitiveness. We then develop a bottom-up aggregation model in which firm capability profiles form national capability stock, intensity, and distribution, while institutions, industrial structure, linkages, and spillovers condition their conversion into national performance in international markets. The framework clarifies firm heterogeneity, strengthens the microfoundations of national competitiveness, and connects strategy, international business, and economics.

title: Competition in a Billion-Dollar Cartel: Strategic Imperatives for Legacy Incumbents and New Entrants in Formula One

detail.title: Competition in a Billion-Dollar Cartel: Strategic Imperatives for Legacy Incumbents and New Entrants in Formula One
detail.abstract: The transformation of the Formula One (F1) motorsport ecosystem following its 2017 acquisition by Liberty Media highlights the managerial implications of engineered resource scarcity. Historically operating as a capital-intensive marketing loss leader where corporate owners deployed annual budgets exceeding 400 million dollars with zero expectation of direct profitability, the introduction of the 2021 financial regulations fundamentally inverted the industry’s economic profile. By implementing a $135 million cost cap, the regulatory framework converted volatile capital sinks into optimized, cash-surplus-generating corporate franchises with an average valuation of 2.31 billion dollars. An analysis of this closed-loop franchise architecture provides explicit strategic prescriptions for two distinct market actors. For legacy incumbents, managers must shift from unconstrained asset accumulation to efficient constraint optimization, systematically leveraging regulatory carve-outs like elite human capital acquisition and transforming trackside hospitality into high-value business-to-business deal-facilitation platforms to secure asymmetric revenue. For prospective new entrants, an evaluation of the defensive economic barriers erected by the Concorde Agreement structure establishes the precise operational and infrastructure parameters required to survive a one billion dollar entry threshold. Ultimately, this study offers critical insights into how institutional rule changes permanently alter competitive strategy and industry dynamics.

title:
How Detectable are AI-generated Peer Review Comments? 
Testing Detection Systems Against Human, AI-generated, AI-polished, and Intentionally Humanised Text

detail.title:
How Detectable are AI-generated Peer Review Comments? 
Testing Detection Systems Against Human, AI-generated, AI-polished, and Intentionally Humanised Text

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This study was conducted on behalf of, and while employed at, the National Health and Medical research Council (NHMRC)
declarations.funderStatement: National Health and Medical research Council (NHMRC)

detail.abstract: The use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in research peer review raises significant confidentiality and integrity concerns, prompting funding agencies including NHMRC and ARC to prohibit AI-assisted assessment of grant applications. However, the detectability of AI-generated peer review comments remains largely untested. This pilot study evaluates thirteen AI-based tools across five authorship conditions representing realistic peer review scenarios: (1) purely human comments, (2) purely AI-generated comments from full applications, (3) human-authored comments polished by AI for grammar and clarity, (4) AI rewrites with style-matching prompts, and (5) AI-generated comments intentionally humanised to reduce detectability. Using a balanced sample of 50 peer review comments (10 per category) from real grant applications processed via enterprise Microsoft Copilot, we assessed detection accuracy, false-positive rates, and category-specific vulnerability patterns. Results show dramatic variability: the bestperforming detector achieved 87.5% AI detection (TP=35/40) with zero false alarms on human text (FP=0/10), while several detectors failed to identify any AI-generated content (TP=0/40). Style-matched AI rewrites (Category 4) proved most consistently difficult to detect, while intentionally humanised text (Category 5) showed the widest variation across systems. These findings demonstrate that most current AI detection systems exhibit insufficient reliability and consistency for high-stakes peer review integrity monitoring, and that hybrid authorship pathways (human-seeded, AI-rewritten) can substantially evade detection.

title: Fiscal Sustainability of Healthcare Systems in Bosnia and Herzegovina: Challenges and Policy Recommendations
affiliations: School of Economics and Business, University of Sarajevo and School of Economics and Business, University of Sarajevo

detail.title: Fiscal Sustainability of Healthcare Systems in Bosnia and Herzegovina: Challenges and Policy Recommendations
detail.abstract: This paper examines the fiscal sustainability of healthcare systems in Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH), focusing on the interplay between financing, expenditure patterns, and care quality. The system is highly fragmented (14 ministries, 13 funds, three legal frameworks). Despite spending over 9% of GDP, BiH records suboptimal outcomes with per-capita health expenditure of 1,477 PPP USD, near the bottom of European rankings. Using National Health Accounts, fund reports, and WHO data (2008-2020), we trace trends and fiscal space. Key challenges include accumulating fund deficits; large regional coverage disparities (56.2% in Canton 10 to 109.3% in Bosnian-Podrinje Canton); high out-of-pocket payments (29.4% of total health expenditure vs 20.9% EU average); hospital bed-occupancy below 60%; and a threefold variation in per-capita insurance outlays across cantons. Revenues are concentrated: 91.7% of Federation HIF income comes from payroll while employees are only 28% of the insured, leaving the model pro-cyclical and vulnerable to demographic and labour-market shocks. Findings show that relatively high spending-to-GDP coexists with low per-capita resources, fragmentation, inefficient allocation, and weak incentives. In response, priority interventions are directed toward spending quality and allocative efficiency rather than simple revenue expansion: rebalancing toward primary and ambulatory care with strengthened strategic purchasing and solidarity-based risk pooling; expenditure rationalisation through higher capacity utilisation, stronger financial management, and performance-based payment; and targeted revenue diversification, most notably VAT differentiation on reimbursable medicines (estimated annual savings €8.5-€29.2 million), together with improved budget transparency and healthmotivated excises, all underpinned by reforms to reduce fragmented governance.

title: Effects of Fringe Benefits on Job Satisfaction: A Study on Employees in Dhaka City
affiliations: Jahangirnagar University - Institute of Business Administration, Jahangirnagar University, Jahangirnagar University - Institute of Business Administration, Jahangirnagar University - Institute of Business Administration, Jahangirnagar University - Institute of Business Administration and Jahangirnagar University - Institute of Business Administration

detail.title: Effects of Fringe Benefits on Job Satisfaction: A Study on Employees in Dhaka City
detail.abstract: Job satisfaction in Bangladesh is primarily influenced by economic status and the provision of fringe benefits, which include tax-free perks such as retirement plans, health insurance, paid time off, and flexible working hours. These benefits are crucial for attracting and retaining talent, enhancing employee satisfaction, and boosting productivity. Research indicates a significant relationship between both financial and non-financial fringe benefits and job happiness, with organizations encouraged to develop effective compensation packages that address diverse employee needs. A study conducted in Dhaka using quantitative methods confirmed these findings, showing that fringe benefits substantially impact job satisfaction, with path coefficients and R-square values supporting the relationship between fringe benefits and job satisfaction.

title: Bitcoin, Property or Money? Reframing the Debate before the High Court
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Bitcoin, Property or Money? Reframing the Debate before the High Court

contentType.other: published as a blog on my website at www.ccgconsultants.com

detail.abstract:
The pending High Court appeal in Poulton v Conrad raises one of the most significant questions yet considered by an Australian court concerning digital assets: whether Bitcoin constitutes property at common law and, if so, whether traditional proprietary remedies such as detinue and conversion are available.

The appeal has attracted competing approaches. The appellant characterises Bitcoin as information recorded on a distributed ledger and argues against proprietary recognition. The respondent emphasises Bitcoin's practical functionality and the control exercised through private keys. The Federal Commissioner of Taxation approaches the issue through established principles of property law and the long-standing taxation treatment of Bitcoin as property. These competing arguments illustrate the continuing difficulty of applying legal concepts developed for physical assets and bilateral legal relationships to decentralised digital assets.

This article examines the competing submissions and argues that the debate is often framed too narrowly. The more fundamental question is not whether Bitcoin is property in the abstract, but how the law should characterise exclusive control over a digitally scarce economic resource. In doing so, the article considers Bitcoin's monetary characteristics, its practical operation through cryptographic authentication, and the distinction between legal title and practical control.

The article further explores the implications of the appeal beyond cryptocurrency, including secured lending, insolvency, taxation, estate administration and the operation of the Personal Property Securities Act 2009 (Cth). It argues that the long-term significance of the appeal may lie less in the classification of Bitcoin as property and more in whether Australian law begins to recognise cryptographic control as a legally significant form of control in its own right.

The article concludes that the future development of digital asset law is likely to depend upon legal frameworks that better align proprietary rights with practical control, particularly where control is exercised through private keys rather than physical possession or contractual rights.

title: The Agent Infrastructure Stack
affiliations: Hashtag Web3

detail.title: The Agent Infrastructure Stack
detail.abstract: Between 2024 and 2026, the AI agent developer toolchain split into eight specialized infrastructure layers, capturing over $13 billion in combined funding. This paper maps these layers, evaluates their dependency dynamics, and identifies six emerging architectural trends. The analysis covers venture databases, SEC filings, and enterprise surveys for over 50 companies. Key findings reveal extreme capital concentration, with the top 10 deals capturing 85% of capital, and the direct acquisition of security and observability providers by major cloud platforms, while compute and perception layers maintain independent technical moats.

title: How Enduring Organizational Values Institutionalize Gender Equity
affiliations: Southern Cross University

detail.title: How Enduring Organizational Values Institutionalize Gender Equity
detail.abstract: This paper uses judo as an instructive organizational analogue to examine how deeply embedded values can sustain gender equity over time. Many organizations adopt equity initiatives in response to external pressure, yet these efforts often remain compliance-oriented and fail to reshape everyday norms, relationships, and systems. By contrast, judo shows how a durable value architecture can normalize inclusive behavior across training, leadership, officiating, competition, and development pathways. The paper argues that values become influential when they are institutionalized through routine practice, shared expectations, and structural design rather than formal policy alone. It develops a values-based perspective on gender equity that links organizational culture, psychological safety, inclusive systems, and sustained behavioral alignment. Its central contribution is practical as well as theoretical: judo offers a concrete model of how organizations can translate stated values into everyday mechanisms that make equity more durable, credible, and behaviorally real.

title: CARS: A Cost-Aware Right-Sizing Framework for Spark Workloads on Azure Databricks
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: CARS: A Cost-Aware Right-Sizing Framework for Spark Workloads on Azure Databricks
detail.abstract: Cost optimization for Spark workloads on managed lakehouse platforms such as Azure Databricks remains under-served by existing literature, which addresses cluster sizing, autoscaling, and transient instance management as separate concerns. We present CARS (Cost-Aware Right-Sizing), a unified framework that formalizes the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) for batch ETL workloads on Azure Databricks as a five-component decomposition incorporating Databricks Unit (DBU) pricing, Azure infrastructure costs, storage tiers, egress, and-distinctively-explicit penalty terms for autoscaling inefficiency, spot instance eviction risk, and resource idleness. We formulate cost-aware right-sizing as a constrained mixed-integer non-linear program and provide a tractable enumeration algorithm with a closed-form subroutine for spot-ratio optimization. Validation against published benchmarks (TPC-DS at 1 TB and 10 TB, HiBench, and a synthetic shuffle-heavy workload) using Azure pricing data shows CARS-selected configurations achieve 40-69% TCO reduction versus default-autoscaling configurations, 14-54% versus the Databricks-recommended spot pattern, and 15-33% versus an OptEx-style cost-optimal baseline that omits inefficiency penalties, while satisfying SLA runtime constraints. We release a reference implementation as open source. The framework generalizes to AWS Databricks via parameter substitution.

title: Pricing Inefficiencies in the Independent Beat Market: Does Branding Quality Predict Pricing Power Among Independent Music Producers?

detail.title: Pricing Inefficiencies in the Independent Beat Market: Does Branding Quality Predict Pricing Power Among Independent Music Producers?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I declare no conflicts of interest. This research was conducted independently with no financial relationships or organizational affiliations that could have influenced the study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study involved no human participants, patients, or identifiable personal data. All data were collected through structured observation of publicly accessible beat marketplace listings. No ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was self-funded as an independent research project.

detail.abstract: The independent digital beat marketplace, in which music producers license instrumental tracks directly to recording artists via platforms such as BeatStars and Traktrain, represents a rapidly growing segment of the creator economy that has received virtually no empirical attention. This study investigates whether observable business signals, principally branding quality and licensing transparency, predict lease pricing power among independent producers. Drawing on an original structured-observation dataset of 112 beat listings collected from BeatStars and Traktrain in 2026, this study finds substantial evidence of pricing inefficiency rooted in information asymmetry and widespread underdevelopment of producer business infrastructure. Producers scoring 3 or above on a 5-point branding scale charge an average of $35.20 per lease compared to $20.86 for low-branding producers, representing a 68.8% differential. Producers with clear licensing terms posted charge $33.17 versus $19.67 for those without, constituting a 68.6% premium. A cumulative business-signal index reveals a near-monotonic doseresponse relationship: producers with three or more observable business signals average $34.35 per lease versus $20.73 for those with zero, a difference of 65.8%. These findings are interpreted through the frameworks of signaling theory (Spence, 1973), experience goods (Nelson, 1970), and adverse selection (Akerlof, 1970), and suggest that targeted business literacy interventions could substantially improve market efficiency and Settipalli (2026) 1 PRICING INEFFICIENCIES IN THE INDEPENDENT BEAT MARKET Settipalli (2026) producer revenue outcomes. Limitations, directions for future research, and practical recommendations are discussed.

title: Comprehensive analysis of food supply in Spain based on the TABULA™ branded food composition database
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Comprehensive analysis of food supply in Spain based on the TABULA™ branded food composition database
detail.abstract: Improving the nutritional quality of food products is a key strategy for advancing public health and encouraging healthier dietary practices. This can be achieved through food reformulation, which involves modifying processing methods and product compositions to enhance beneficial nutrients while reducing components associated with negative health outcomes. To monitor these developments within the Spanish food market, TABULA™, an updated branded food composition database, was developed and systematically expanded. A comprehensive descriptive analysis was performed using the first release of the database, which contains information on more than 6,500 pre-packaged food and beverage products marketed in Spain between January 2022 and November 2023. Data were meticulously collected from product labels of both branded and private-label items available through major online retail platforms. Products were classified according to the World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Office for Europe nutrient profiling model to facilitate nutritional assessment and comparison. The study primarily aimed to identify the mandatory nutritional components declared on food labels to ensure compliance with current regulatory requirements. The findings provide valuable insights into food composition, nutrition labeling practices, and reformulation trends within the Spanish food sector, thereby supporting future food monitoring initiatives and evidence-based public health policies.

title: What do we need to know about biodiversity in Economics and Business?
affiliations: , Middlesex University and Faculty of Business, Lingnan University

detail.title: What do we need to know about biodiversity in Economics and Business?
detail.abstract: Purpose: The purpose of this study is to comprehensively review biodiversity-related research within the realms of business, economics, and management from 1993 to 2025. We assess the theoretical underpinnings, intellectual structure, and evolution of the field. It aims to pinpoint crucial theoretical shifts and identify persistent research gaps, focusing on the integration of stakeholder and legitimacy theories, and ecological economics within biodiversity research, while highlighting the shortcomings in addressing corporate accountability and the complexities of biodiversity financialisation. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study utilises bibliometric mapping and systematic literature reviews to explore biodiversity research across business and economic disciplines. We extracted data from Scopus, incorporating articles, books, and conference papers that focus on biodiversity challenges from economic and business perspectives. Using VOSviewer and R for bibliometric analysis, we created visual networks of the intellectual structure and thematic clusters in the field, which allowed for a detailed examination of the evolution and impact of research over time, identifying both influential studies and prominent research gaps. Findings: The findings reveal an increasing alignment of biodiversity research with ecological economics, legitimacy, and stakeholder theories. The research highlights a critical shift from firm-level strategies to systemic transformation needs within economic and financial frameworks, advocating for integrated approaches to biodiversity governance. However, challenges persist, notably in the areas of addressing power asymmetries and corporate greenwashing. Despite a growing emphasis on ecosystem services valuation, the market-based logic frequently overlooks crucial ecological interdependencies and socio-ecological complexities. Originality/Value: The study contributes to the field by offering a structured, theory-driven agenda for future biodiversity research, emphasising the need for universal governance frameworks that transcend traditional firm-level approaches. It uniquely challenges the reductionist market-based logics prevalent in ecosystem services valuation. It calls for a rethinking of economic and financial paradigms to ensure the safeguarding of biodiversity as a core component of economic resilience and planetary stability. A comprehensive bibliometric approach and synthesis of theoretical advancements provide a novel perspective on integrating biodiversity considerations into broader economic and corporate frameworks.

title: Estimating Demand in the Absence of Sales and Inventory Information
affiliations: Indian School of Business - Operations Management, Indian School of Business and City University of New York (CUNY) - Narendra Paul Loomba Department of Management

detail.title: Estimating Demand in the Absence of Sales and Inventory Information
detail.abstract: Nanostores, the backbone of the retail sector in many emerging economies, face unique operational challenges. These include liquidity and shelf-space constraints, and lack of IT infrastructure such as point-of-sale devices. Consequently, upstream partners responsible for replenishment (such as a manufacturer or its agent) do not have access to sales data and must rely on historical replenishment data to estimate customer demand for replenishment planning. However, replenishment data are subject to two distortions: (i) demand-to-sales distortion due to stockouts, i.e., censoring, and (ii) sales-to-replenishment distortion caused by the retailer's inventory policy. The latter is amplified because nanostores operate at a small scale, while inventory is replenished in relatively large batch sizes. We develop a parsimonious model of the nanostore's inventory dynamics using a modified base-stock policy: the nanostore receives replenishments in batches to reach a target inventory level. Using this model as the data generating process for the replenishment data, we construct a distribution of the unobserved inventory and sales data. We employ the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm to jointly estimate the parameters of the demand distribution and the target inventory level. We find that the EM algorithm misattributes stockouts in some periods involving the maximum observed replenishment quantity and therefore systematically underestimates the target inventory level and correspondingly overestimates the demand. We further show that augmenting the replenishment data with a binary stockout indicator can almost eliminate the upward bias in the demand estimate. Finally, we show that this bias correction can help the upstream partners significantly reduce their visit frequency to the nanostore without adversely impacting the cycle service levels. Our results suggest that manufacturers and distributors can significantly reduce the cost of replenishment to nanostores by more accurately estimating the retail demand with little additional information (i.e., stockout indicators) without making heavy investments in digitization of nanostores with sophisticated POS or inventory management tools.

title: Leveraging Trade Credit to Expand Informal Consumer Credit in Base-of-the-Pyramid Retail
affiliations: Tilburg University - Tilburg University School of Economics and Management, Arizona State University (ASU) - Supply Chain Management, University of Colorado at Boulder - Leeds School of Business, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Center for Transportation & Logistics and Tilburg University - Tilburg University School of Economics and Management

detail.title: Leveraging Trade Credit to Expand Informal Consumer Credit in Base-of-the-Pyramid Retail
detail.abstract:
Problem definition: Informal credit is extended by small independent grocery retailers ("nanostores") to billions of base-of-the-pyramid consumers. We study whether supplier trade credit enables liquidity-constrained nanostore shopkeepers to extend more informal credit to such liquidity-constrained consumers. 

Methodology/results: Through a field experiment with nanostores in Lima, Peru, we find that access to trade credit partly increases the likelihood of consumer credit provision. To understand the behavioral underpinnings of this result, we develop an analytical model in which shopkeepers allocate limited working capital between base consumers, who always pay immediately upon arrival, and additional credit consumers, who pay later but carry default risk. The model predicts that relaxing working capital constraints through trade credit should increase optimal consumer credit provision, with negligible risk of supplier default when credit consumers are profitable on average. We subsequently test these predictions in a behavioral experiment and find systematic deviations from the theoretical benchmark. Participants exhibit mental accounting so that they become more conservative when working capital includes trade credit, discount trade credit more heavily than their own funds, fail to calibrate consumer credit provision  - offering too little (much) when the risk is low (high) - and fail to expand consumer credit provision even when effective capital increases. Examining the heterogeneity of the effect, we find that participants with a positive attitude toward credit are more willing to allocate both trade credit funds and their own working capital toward consumer credit provision. Finally, a simple change in repayment-penalty framing mitigates this mental-accounting effect. 

Managerial implications: Together, the results highlight the challenges shopkeepers face when extending consumer credit and point to behavioral frictions-particularly a repayment shortfall aversion-that would need to be addressed to enhance the pass-through of trade credit to end consumers.

title: Reducing Food Waste Through Profit-Driven Digital Applications
affiliations: University of West Attica

detail.title: Reducing Food Waste Through Profit-Driven Digital Applications
detail.abstract: This paper examines the contribution of new technologies in reducing food waste through real, profit-driven applications in the retail and food service sectors. Based on data from the UN and Eurostat, the environmental and economic footprint of the problem in Greece and the EU is analyzed. Through the description of the Too Good To Go platform, it is highlighted how digital tools provide economic incentives to businesses for managing surplus food. In conclusion, it is proven that technological innovation can successfully align business profitability with environmental sustainability.

title: Regulatory Fragmentation, Disclosure Interpretability, and ESG Rating Divergence
affiliations: University of Queensland, Macquarie University and Macquarie University - Department of Applied Finance and Actuarial Studies

detail.title: Regulatory Fragmentation, Disclosure Interpretability, and ESG Rating Divergence

keywords: And ESG Rating Divergence Regulatory Fragmentation

detail.abstract: We examine the informational consequences of firms' regulatory environments for outside ESG evaluation. We argue that divergence across ESG rating agencies reflects not only differences in scope and measurement, but also variation in how tightly disclosures constrain interpretation. When overlapping regulatory regimes weaken interpretive constraint, the same information set may support a broader range of defensible mappings into ESG assessments. Using U.S. public firms from 2001 to 2022, we find that regulatory fragmentation is associated with greater cross-provider ESG rating divergence, and this relation is robust to alternative divergence measures, alternative rating harmonization procedures, and supplementary identification tests. Disclosure-based analyses show that fragmentation is associated with more qualified, litigious, and uncertainty-laden language in mandatory filings, and that the fragmentation-associated components of these features are positively related to subsequent divergence. The relation is weaker in the presence of shareholder attention and sustainability committees. Collectively, the findings suggest that fragmented oversight weakens the common interpretive anchor available to ESG evaluators.

title: AutoFactory Dataset to Support AI in Manufacturing Systems
affiliations: Cadi Ayyad University, Cadi Ayyad University and Cadi Ayyad University

detail.title: AutoFactory Dataset to Support AI in Manufacturing Systems
detail.abstract:
Automating code generation in manufacturing systems requires Artificial Intelligence (AI) models capable of interpreting textual requirement specifications. One of the main challenges is the absence of publicly available, domain-specific datasets suitable for training such models. This article presents AutoFactory, an open-source dataset that includes manually written and LLM-augmented requirement specifications, annotated by domain experts for Named Entity Recognition (NER) tasks using the BIO format.
AutoFactory enables the extraction and classification of key industrial components, including actuators, pre-actuators, sensors, effectors, and others. These elements correspond to real-world input and output signals in manufacturing systems. The dataset is grounded in realistic scenarios built with Factory I/O and includes 3D scenes, tag tables, and screenshots captured from multiple camera perspectives. To enhance linguistic diversity while preserving semantic intent, all specifications were expanded using large language models and evaluated through semantic similarity analysis (average cosine similarity above 0.92), complemented by manual validation to ensure consistency.
To facilitate the annotation process, a custom labeling tool was developed. It runs locally to preserve data privacy and provides a user-friendly interface. The tool is adaptable to a wide range of NER tasks and allows researchers to customize labels for different domains by adding or modifying tags.
To assess the practical value of the dataset, transformer-based models such as BERT and DistilBERT were fine-tuned on the annotated requirement specifications. The highest-performing model reached an F1-score of 0.95, confirming the dataset’s ability to support accurate identification of key components in manufacturing systems.
This combination of human expertise and AI-based augmentation provides a robust foundation for training AI systems to interpret manufacturing behaviors from text. AutoFactory contributes to ongoing research efforts aimed at enabling intelligent systems to assist in generating control code from requirement specifications, reducing reliance on manual programming in industrial automation.
