title: Managerial Readiness for AI-Enabled Marketing Decision Systems
affiliations: Manhattan University and Columbia University

detail.title: Managerial Readiness for AI-Enabled Marketing Decision Systems
detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping marketing decision-making, yet the readiness of marketing managers to adopt and apply AI remains underexplored. This conceptual paper develops a multidimensional framework of managerial AI readiness, integrating perceived usefulness, data literacy, organizational support, trust in AI, ethical concern, and self-efficacy. Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model, the Technology-Organization-Environment framework, and social cognitive theory, the paper synthesizes literature and advances theory-driven propositions to guide future research and practice. The model proposes how cognitive, organizational, and ethical factors interact to influence self-efficacy and, in turn, readiness to adopt AI in marketing. The study contributes by extending existing adoption theories with psychological and ethical dimensions, offering a manager-centric perspective often missing in AI research. For practitioners, the framework provides a diagnostic tool to identify capability gaps and guide targeted interventions such as training, culturebuilding, and ethical governance. The paper offers actionable insights for organizations, policymakers, and AI vendors seeking to foster responsible and confident AI adoption in marketing contexts.

title: Structural Causality in Genesis 2-3: A Problem Solving and Corrective Action Approach to the Eden Narrative
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Structural Causality in Genesis 2-3: A Problem Solving and Corrective Action Approach to the Eden Narrative
detail.abstract: This study proposes an interdisciplinary approach to biblical exegesis by applying the principles of Problem Solving and Corrective Action (PSCA), a quality management and systems analysis methodology, to the narrative of the human fall in Genesis 2-3. Scholarly discussions of the Eden narrative have long engaged questions concerning the causal structure of the transgression, the function of divine non-intervention during the temptation, and the theological significance of the subsequent judicial decrees. The present study employs the PSCA framework as a heuristic analytical model rather than as a claim regarding the historical intent or compositional methodology of the Genesis author, utilizing contemporary systems analysis to illuminate structural and causal relationships within the biblical text. The investigation proceeds in two stages. First, an Ishikawa (fishbone) analysis identifies contributing factors across the categories of Agent, Method, Measurement, Material, and Environment. Second, a Three-Legged Five Why (3L5Y) investigation traces causal relationships through the interconnected dimensions of the Specific Problem, Detection Failure, and Systemic Failure. This interdisciplinary model is integrated with close literary and lexical analysis of the Hebrew text and supplemented by formal logical representation to examine the coherence of the proposed causal architecture. The study argues that the Eden narrative may be understood as portraying the primordial transgression within an intentionally open covenantal framework in which authentic relationship presupposes genuine human freedom and, consequently, the structural possibility of nonconformance. Within this interpretive model, the divine judgments following the fall function analogously to short-term containment measures, while the proto-evangelium of Genesis 3:15 serves as the narrative's long-term corrective action directed toward the restoration of covenantal and cosmic order. By integrating quality management theory, systems analysis, formal logic, and biblical exegesis, this study offers a novel methodological framework for examining the structural dynamics of the Genesis narrative and demonstrates the potential value of interdisciplinary analytical models for theological interpretation.

title: Should Demand Models Incorporate Competitor Prices? Oblivious Learning and Algorithmic Collusion
affiliations: Columbia University - Columbia Business School, Decision Risk and Operations and Columbia University - Columbia Business School, Decision Risk and Operations

detail.title: Should Demand Models Incorporate Competitor Prices? Oblivious Learning and Algorithmic Collusion
detail.abstract: On a platform with many sellers, should a pricing algorithm explicitly model competitors' prices when learning demand? Classical learning arguments suggest an affirmative answer: ignoring competitors induces model misspecification and inefficiency. In contrast, recent work on algorithmic collusion suggests that strategic obliviousness---deliberately ignoring competitor prices---may facilitate collusive outcomes and improve profits. We study this modeling choice in a stylized competitive market with unknown noisy demand, in which multiple sellers repeatedly set prices and estimate demand via iterated least squares, and either incorporate competitors' prices into their demand models (informed) or ignore them (oblivious). We first show that, relative to a monopolist, an oblivious seller in a competitive market must explore more aggressively to compensate for the loss of dynamic competitor information. Building on this insight, we characterize market dynamics when all sellers are oblivious and show that prices converge to the competitive outcome under sufficient exploration, while a continuum of pseudo-equilibria arises when exploration decays. Analyzing the resulting price trajectories, we uncover an excursion phenomenon that gives rise to transient collusive patterns that dissipate as learning progresses. In markets with both oblivious and informed sellers, the informed strictly out-earn the oblivious. Read as a strategy game, the modeling choice has a unique Nash equilibrium: the all-informed market, in which prices converge to the competitive outcome efficiently. Overall, our results indicate that collusive patterns are not robust and are not sustained by oblivious modeling; therefore, incorporating competitor information, together with sufficient price exploration, remains a reliable strategy for sellers in competitive markets.

title: Who Invited the Lawyer? Essential Qualifications of Modern General Counsels

detail.title: Who Invited the Lawyer? Essential Qualifications of Modern General Counsels

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares they have no personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study was approved and conducted in accordance with an Institutional Review Board protocol. Study participants executed a written consent prior to their participation.

detail.abstract: In the view of many institutional stakeholders, the lawyers are everywhere. As liability concerns permeate organizational decision making, decision makers increasingly rely on their in-house lawyers. Limited empirical research has considered what qualifies attorneys-typically individuals with little-to-no experience as institutional administrators-to accrue executive-level status and influence in matters of legal, legal-adjacent, and extra-legal concern. To better understand the qualities and qualifications of modern general counsels (GCs), an empirical qualitative multiple case study was conducted in the complex institutional context of U.S. research universities to understand the expansive influence of their GCs. The cases of six highly experienced, incumbent GCs were explored to understand how GCs perceive and experience the skills, qualities, and experiences that qualify them for such a highly influential executive role. The findings revealed 15 discrete GC role qualifications distributed among four categories: (1) technical skills and competencies, (2) dispositional qualities, (3) relational abilities, and (4) executive capacities. A new conceptual framework is proposed, depicting the qualities and qualifications of modern GCs and the relationship of these qualities and qualifications to GCs' exercise of executive influence.

title: A Computational Model for Risk-based Quality Governance Assessment in High-risk Infrastructure Projects: A Weighted Composite Scoring Approach
affiliations: University of Essex

detail.title: A Computational Model for Risk-based Quality Governance Assessment in High-risk Infrastructure Projects: A Weighted Composite Scoring Approach
detail.abstract: High-risk infrastructure projects, characterized by their complexity, substantial investment, and extended timelines, necessitate robust quality governance frameworks to mitigate potential failures and ensure successful delivery [1]. Traditional governance models often struggle to integrate the dynamic interplay of risk factors with quality assurance mechanisms across the project lifecycle. This paper introduces a computational model designed for risk-based quality governance assessment in such projects. The model employs a weighted composite scoring approach, systematically evaluating various dimensions of quality governance against identified project-specific risks. It synthesizes quantitative metrics and qualitative indicators, transforming complex risk landscapes into actionable governance scores. The methodology encompasses indicator selection, an algorithm for composite score calculation, and a multi-stage validation process. Application through simulated case studies demonstrates the model's capacity to provide a nuanced, real-time assessment of governance efficacy, identifying vulnerabilities and guiding strategic interventions. This approach supports project stakeholders in making informed decisions, thereby enhancing project resilience and reducing the likelihood of adverse outcomes. The model contributes a structured, quantifiable method for proactively managing quality governance in critical infrastructure developments. To operate this concept, the proposed model integrates governance indicators, risk criticality metrics, and decision-weighting mechanisms within a computational decision-support architecture. Specifically, the model combines expert-derived governance indicators with probabilistic risk assessment to compute a normalized Weighted Composite Score (WCS) representing governance effectiveness under risk exposure. Sensitivity analysis and Monte Carlo simulation are incorporated to evaluate the robustness of governance scoring under uncertain project conditions. This computational structure enables systematic benchmarking of governance performance across infrastructure projects with varying risk profiles.

title: Revealing the Right Wrongs: Norm Violations Involving Unconventional Behaviors Boost Leader Authenticity and Voter Support
affiliations: ESADE Business School, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Dresden University and University of Vienna

detail.title: Revealing the Right Wrongs: Norm Violations Involving Unconventional Behaviors Boost Leader Authenticity and Voter Support
detail.abstract: Although norm violators are typically censured, leaders and politicians often publicly selfdisclose past norm violations. Could such revelations be strategically advantageous? Across five studies, we examine whether disclosing prior norm violations enhances leaders' perceived authenticity and downstream support. We distinguish unconventional norm violations (e.g., wearing sweatpants to a black-tie event) from antisocial violations (e.g., nepotism), personal vulnerabilities (e.g., being mugged), and neutral self-disclosures (e.g., hobbies), holding negativity constant across conditions. Results show that leaders who disclosed unconventional norm violations were perceived as significantly more authentic than leaders who disclosed other types of information. Importantly, this authenticity boost was unique to voluntary self-disclosure: it disappeared when identical information was revealed through media reports (Study 1) or direct observation (Study 2), highlighting the critical role of intentional revelation. Further, the effect was stronger for leaders than for non-leaders (Study 3), suggesting that leaders can leverage accumulated idiosyncrasy credits to come clean about prior misgivings in ways that signal authenticity rather than deviance. Finally, perceptions of authenticity translated into meaningful behavioral outcomes: leaders who disclosed unconventional violations received greater support and endorsement than comparison leaders (Studies 4a-4b). Our findings demonstrate that not all norm violations are equal and that unconventional violations, when selfdisclosed by leaders, can function as a reputational asset rather than a liability. This research advances counter-normative influence theory by identifying perceived authenticity as a novel psychological mechanism linking norm violations to positive outcomes, and by clarifying when and for whom norm violations can increase, rather than decrease, leader endorsement.

detail.abstract: Within corporate workplaces, Human Resource (HR) professionals balance a range of responsibilities, spanning employee wellbeing, recruitment, and administrative tasks. Given the digitalization of their roles and the increased focus on employee wellbeing since COVID-19, HR professionals are prone to stress and burnout, especially in large workplaces. There is a lack of research with HR professionals across India focusing on their experience of stress and coping within their roles. This study aimed to understand the nature of stress faced by Indian HR professionals and strategies they use to cope. Using a mixed methods design, stress levels and common coping strategies were assessed, while interviews provided detailed insight into personal experiences. 79% of HR professionals experienced moderate or high stress. Common stressors included work-related demands, boundary-related challenges, and interpersonal challenges. Organizational culture and personal adaptive or coping styles have the potential to reduce stress. HRs largely used independent ways to cope with challenges. They commonly engaged in active coping, acceptance, and positive reframing to cope with stress, yet there was a relation between higher perceived stress and engaging in negative coping strategies such as behavioral disengagement and self-blame. As stigma around mental health persists, leadership must implement specialized support for HR professionals to facilitate usage of workplace mental health services.

title: Connecting Internal Branding with Employee Brand Performance
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and OSSIAM

detail.title: Connecting Internal Branding with Employee Brand Performance
detail.abstract: Purpose-Although, there is evidence that internal branding (IB) influences and effects employees' brand-supportive behaviors, it is still unknown what determines employees' brand performance (EBP). Moreover, a mediator is assessed in relation to how IB practices affect EBP. Design/methodology/approach-The study examines the banking sector in Pakistan, the authors performed Partial Least Squares (PLS) to analyze 426 bank staff data. Findings-The results reveal that an effective IB strategy leverages EBP and BC. However, brand trust and brand identification do not directly leverage EBP. Practical implication: By incorporating brand attitudes and implementing a robust IB strategy, firms can enhance EBP. These initiatives are not just the sole responsibility of the brand manager, but instead a collective responsibility of all employees at all levels. Managers of financial services firms are recommended to pursue IB strategy actively rather than let it become a passive function of human resources. Originality/value-This research fills a gap in our understanding by bringing together two underresearched areas in the banking industry namely, IB and EBP. It reveals the significance of creating an internal brand at a corporate level and also proposes the antecedents of EBP and clarifies the relationships among them. This research lends credence to the idea that implementing IB might be a valuable strategy that can be used by service firms in their efforts to better their staff's brand performance.

title: Enabler or impediment? ESG practices and green innovation in Chinese manufacturing firms: A longitudinal study under visibility
affiliations: School of Management, Xian Jiaotong University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Enabler or impediment? ESG practices and green innovation in Chinese manufacturing firms: A longitudinal study under visibility
detail.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the relationship between environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices and organizational performance (OP), focusing on the mediating role of organizational green innovation (OGI) and the moderating role of organizational visibility (OV). ESG practices have emerged as strategic mechanisms through which organizations pursue sustainable innovation and long-term competitiveness. Drawing on stakeholder theory, the resource-based view (RBV), natural resource-based view (NRBV), and institutional theory, the study analyzes longitudinal panel data from 752 Chinese manufacturing firms comprising 18,716 firm-year observations (2001-2025) using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings demonstrate that ESG practices significantly enhance organizational green innovation and organizational performance, while organizational green innovation partially mediates the ESG-performance relationship, highlighting innovation as a key mechanism through which ESG creates organizational value. Furthermore, organizational visibility negatively moderates the direct relationship between ESG and performance, indicating that heightened stakeholder scrutiny and legitimacy pressures reduce performance benefits derived from ESG initiatives, even as ESG engagement itself remains beneficial. Robustness analyses across state-owned and private enterprises confirm the stability of these findings, with private firms demonstrating stronger green innovation-to-performance conversion. These findings reveal that while ESG practices enable green innovation and knowledge creation, the moderating role of organizational visibility operates primarily as a negative boundary condition on the direct ESG-performance pathway. The findings also provide practical implications for managers and policymakers seeking to leverage ESG-driven innovation to support sustainable industrial transformation and contribute to SDG 9 (industry, innovation, and infrastructure) and SDG 12 (responsible consumption and production) in emerging economies.

title: Heterogeneity in Consumers' Economic Expectations across Euro Area Countries
affiliations: Leibniz University Hannover, National Bank of Slovakia, Leibniz  Universität Hannover and Bank of Finland - Research

detail.title: Heterogeneity in Consumers' Economic Expectations across Euro Area Countries
detail.abstract: This paper examines crosscountry differences in consumer expectations about macroeconomic outcomes and mortgage borrowing conditions within a monetary union. Using harmonized microdata from the ECB Consumer Expectations Survey for eleven euro area countries, we document significant national disparities. By sequentially adding a rich set of consumer-and country-specific macro controls to pooled regressions with country fixed effects, we find that these factors account for much, but not all, of the crosscountry heterogeneity in expectations. These remaining differences likely reflect unobserved countryspecific factors, highlighting the need for country-tailored monetary policy communication to effectively stabilize consumer expectations.

title: Innovation without Borders? The Geography of Technological Diffusion
affiliations: European Central Bank (ECB), Harvard University - Business School (HBS), Goethe University Frankfurt, European Central Bank (ECB), University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) and European Central Bank (ECB)

detail.title: Innovation without Borders? The Geography of Technological Diffusion
detail.abstract: How well does innovation diffuse across geographic boundaries? To shed light on this question, we present a large-scale field experiment involving 3,300 firms across twelve European Union countries. We elicit firms' perceptions of the share of similar firms in their own country that had invested in artificial intelligence (AI), as well as the corresponding share among similar firms in Germany, France, and Italy. We randomly provide half of the sample with accurate information about both domestic and foreign AI investment. We show that firms substantially underestimate competitors' current AI investment, both domestically and abroad, and that they update their expectations about competitors' future AI investment in response to the information treatment. The treatment also causes a statistically significant increase in firms' own expected AI investment rate (p-value < 0.001). We find strong strategic complementarities within borders: a 1 pp increase in the expected share of domestic peers investing in AI raises a firm's own expected AI investment rate by 0.570 pp. These complementarities are absent across borders: the effect of an increase in the expected share of foreign peers investing in AI on a firm's own expected AI investment rate is statistically insignificant. Overall, our evidence shows that innovation diffusion and strategic complementarities in AI investment are much stronger domestically than internationally.

detail.title: Moral Progress in Legal Doctrine

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Tort Law, Vol. 19, No. 1, pp. 43-77, 2026 [10.1515/jtl-2025-0011]
Texas A&M University School of Law Legal Studies Research Paper

detail.abstract: This article integrates the concept of moral progresshere, moral improvement in the thinking and behavior of individuals over timeinto the study of legal doctrine. The article first presents a naturalistic account of what moral progress is and describes three of its most historically and analytically important forms: (1) moral circle expansion, (2) moral domain expansion, and (3) increasing sensitivity to proportionality. The article then analyzes three historical developments in U.S. tort law that qualify as instances of moral progress: (1) the partial demise of the "suicide rule" beginning around the 1980s (according to the article, an episode of moral circle expansion), (2) the liberalization of recovery for emotional harm in the negligent infliction tort beginning around the 1970s (moral domain expansion), and (3) the near-total replacement of contributory negligence by comparative negligence throughout the twentieth century (increasing sensitivity to proportionality). The article ends by outlining three legal scholarly implications of the analysis. (1) Legal scholars may be able to use the concept of moral progress as a criterion for making internal as opposed to external criticisms of tort law. (2) Attending to historical moral progress in an area of law facilitates sounder assessment of the area's present-day moral value. (3) Studying moral progress in legal doctrine can identify open legal historical questions about historical legal actors' motives. More generally, this article can inform legal scholars who seek to analyze morally progressive or regressive change in any area of law.

title: EMOTIF: A Real-World Facial Emotion Recognition Dataset
affiliations: Mohammed V University of Rabat National School of Computer Science and Systems Analysis, Mohammed V University of Rabat National School of Computer Science and Systems Analysis, Mohammed V University of Rabat National School of Computer Science and Systems Analysis and International University of Rabat

detail.title: EMOTIF: A Real-World Facial Emotion Recognition Dataset
detail.abstract: Facial expression recognition remains a core challenge in computer vision, but it's becoming more important in security, adaptive learning, mental health evaluation, and interactive systems. Deep learning models work well, but genuine progress is still restricted by the fact that existing datasets typically don't show the full range and complexity of real-world emotional expressions. A lot of them had unbalanced emotion classifications, not enough variety in context, and were collected in very controlled settings that don't reflect how things are in the real world. A lot of benchmarks just look at Ekman's six main feelings. This limits the range and difficulty that models need to work well in real life. To solve these difficulties, we provide EMOTIF, a collection of real-world facial expressions that shows 15 different emotions in diverse settings. Using advanced detection and annotation methods, an automated processing system created accurate and full emotion data. The FYOLOv5 model (Face: You Only Look Once) is a fast, first-pass detector that performs well for identifying faces in real time and in tough settings. This is basically what it does. Because of this, YOLOv11, a more complex model, makes bounding box predictions better, making sure that face areas are retrieved correctly and with a lot of information. This hybrid detection method creates a well-organized, full dataset that is a great starting point for building reliable, context-aware face emotion recognition algorithms and for making affective computing applications work better in real life.

title: Interactive Effects of Emotional Involvement and Expected Value on Moral Decision-Making: Evidence for Sex Differences from tDCS
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Henan University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Interactive Effects of Emotional Involvement and Expected Value on Moral Decision-Making: Evidence for Sex Differences from tDCS
detail.abstract: The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) has been implicated in both emotional processing and value-based evaluation during moral decision-making, yet its causal role in integrating these processes remains unclear. This experiment tested two hypotheses: first, that the mPFC causally mediates a dynamic shift between emotional and value-based processing; second, that this neural mechanism differs between female and male participants. Seventy-two participants (36 female, 36 male) completed a moral decision-making task involving personal and impersonal moral dilemmas while receiving 25-minute cathodal or sham transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) over the mPFC. Expected value was manipulated through magnitude. Results showed that cathodal tDCS reduced utilitarian tendencies under conditions of low emotional involvement and high expected value, whereas it increased utilitarian tendencies under conditions of high emotional involvement and low expected value. These effects were observed only in female participants. The findings indicate that the mPFC plays a causal and context-dependent role in moral decision-making by dynamically integrating emotional involvement and value-based information. Furthermore, sex-specific effects suggest partially distinct neural mechanisms in female and male participants during moral judgment. These results advance understanding of the brain–cognition mechanisms underlying moral decision-making by demonstrating how the mPFC flexibly reweights emotional and value-related information across moral contexts.

title: Does Supply Chain Innovation Curb Corporate Greenwashing? Evidence from China
affiliations: Guangxi University, Guangxi University, Guangxi University and Yunnan University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Does Supply Chain Innovation Curb Corporate Greenwashing? Evidence from China
detail.abstract: Against the backdrop of the green and low-carbon transition, corporate greenwashing has emerged as a major challenge for environmental governance, reflecting a gap between firms’ green claims and their actual environmental actions. Using panel data from Chinese A-share listed firms in Shanghai and Shenzhen from 2013 to 2023, this study treats the Supply Chain Innovation and Application Pilot Policy launched in 2018 as a quasi-natural experiment and applies a continuous difference-in-differences approach to examine how supply chain innovation affects corporate greenwashing. The results show that supply chain innovation significantly curbs corporate greenwashing, and this finding remains robust across a series of robustness checks. Further analysis suggests that supply chain innovation curbs greenwashing mainly by improving information transparency, strengthening external monitoring, and enhancing firms’ sustained green innovation capability. The effect is more pronounced among non-state-owned enterprises, capital-intensive firms, and firms whose executives have stronger green cognition. This study provides new empirical evidence on the formation and governance of corporate greenwashing from the perspective of digital supply chain governance, and offers useful implications for aligning supply chain innovation policies with firms’ green transformation.

title: Responsible AI for Discretionary Spend Governance in Large Organizations: A Bounded, Assumption-Testing Framework with Human Authority

detail.title: Responsible AI for Discretionary Spend Governance in Large Organizations: A Bounded, Assumption-Testing Framework with Human Authority
detail.abstract: As artificial intelligence enters enterprise spend governance, two questions matter for the Responsible AI community: where AI should operate, and how it should behave where it does. This paper presents a framework with four design pillars. Three-bounded application domain, preserved human authority, and full auditability-operationalize established Responsible AI principles for spend governance. The fourth is new: AI should test the assumptions behind a spend request, not the decision-maker who submitted it. The framework integrates with enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems through three intelligence lenses-demand, rate, and specification-that surface stale assumptions in discretionary spend requests. Informed by anonymized enterprise deployments, the framework generalizes to any rule-bounded discretionary domain where AI must inform, but never replace, human judgment.

title: How Efficient is the Incubation Value Chain Model in Promoting Youth Agribusiness? Evidence from the Youth-Oriented Outreach Resource Training Centers in Eastern DR Congo
affiliations: International Institute of Tropical Agriculture, affiliation not provided to SSRN, International Institute of Tropical Agriculture, Independent Researcher, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, International Institute of Tropical Agriculture, International Institute of Tropical Agriculture, affiliation not provided to SSRN and International Institute of Tropical Agriculture

detail.title: How Efficient is the Incubation Value Chain Model in Promoting Youth Agribusiness? Evidence from the Youth-Oriented Outreach Resource Training Centers in Eastern DR Congo
detail.abstract: Despite efforts to reduce youth unemployment through agribusiness incubations, significant gaps persist globally and in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) regarding the efficiency of the incubation value chain model in promoting youth in agribusiness. The study hypothesizes that incubation is most effective when aligning participants with value chains and fostering networks. It examines the effectiveness of the incubation value chain model through Youth-Oriented Outreach Resource Training Centers–Business Incubators (YORTC-BIs) in eastern DRC. It represents the first study conceptualizing YORTC-BIs as value chain architects rather than organizational structures. Using a sample of 310 youths, the study applies descriptive statistics and logistic regression to evaluate the determinants of youth participation in YORTC-BIs, while Oaxaca–Blinder decomposition assessed gender and spatial disparities. A quasi-experimental design combined with enterprise turnover growth analysis and propensity score matching assesses the impact of YORTC-BIs engagement in agribusiness and incubator efficiency compared to non-participants. Network analysis examines incubators’ interaction across value chain segments. Findings indicate that youth engagement in agribusiness is driven by training, assets, role models, and social networks, with gender and regional disparities. Participation in YORTC-BIs increases the likelihood of engagement by 56%, while incubated youth active across multiple value chain segments achieve 23% higher performance. Network analysis shows growing interconnections within the agribusiness system, with production as the central node. Value chain-oriented incubation models outperform standardized approaches, suggesting that context-sensitive, network-based strategies are essential for promoting inclusive agribusiness development and youth employment in fragile economic contexts.

title: Portfolio Choice with Competing Precautionary and Accumulation Goals
affiliations: Columbia University,  and Columbia University - Department of Industrial Engineering and Operations Research

detail.title: Portfolio Choice with Competing Precautionary and Accumulation Goals
detail.abstract: We study optimal portfolio choice for a household simultaneously managing a random-deadline goal, such as a medical emergency or job loss, and a fixed-deadline goal such as retirement or college tuition. Under a forced funding rule, in which each goal is paid in full whenever affordable, the household maximizes a weighted sum of the probabilities of fully funding both goals in a Black–Scholes market. We identify two novel effects absent from single-goal models: a growth crowding-out effect, in which precautionary saving for the random goal distorts investment toward the fixed goal, and a deadline pressure effect, in which a compressed saving horizon forces excess risk-taking. A striking implication is that the value function need not be monotone in wealth: a household just above the random-goal threshold is forced to pay it when the shock arrives, depleting its wealth for the fixed goal, and ends up worse off than a slightly poorer household that missed the random goal but kept its wealth intact. This non-monotonicity is absent from all single-goal benchmarks and arises purely from the interaction between the two goal types under forced funding. We further study an optional funding variant in which the household may decline the fixed-deadline goal at time T rather than being required to fund it. We characterize the ex ante option value, i.e., the full time-0 value of this flexibility and the terminal option value, i.e., its value at the funding decision node. We find that both options are most valuable at intermediate wealth levels where paying the fixed-deadline goal would substantially reduce the continuation value of the random-deadline problem.

title: Mathematical Foundations of the Circular Economy

detail.title: Mathematical Foundations of the Circular Economy
detail.abstract: We develop a competitive theory of circular economies. Commodities are indexed by physical material and quality state, so that residuals, recovered inputs, and virgin inputs are distinct economic objects. Feasibility requires material balance and residual routing: residual flows generated by households and firms must re-enter recovery rather than disappear through free disposal. Under convexity, bounded attainability, no-free-profit, and a circular Hawkins-Simon productiveness condition, a circular competitive equilibrium exists. On a normalized-throughput feasible set, the circularity-efficiency frontier is decreasing and concave, and its slope is the shadow value of the circularity constraint. Irreversible recovery, finite exogenous energy, and positive replacement needs imply an entropy bound: stationary circularity is bounded away from one under strictly lossy recovery. Finally, regular supported circular optima can be decentralized by commodity prices, residual charges, recovery credits, and lump-sum transfers. The framework connects general equilibrium theory, input-output material balance, and the thermodynamic limits of recycling.

title: Making Bad News Acceptable: Disclosure Design under Information Avoidance
affiliations: The University of Sydney - School of Economics

detail.title: Making Bad News Acceptable: Disclosure Design under Information Avoidance
detail.abstract: Organizations often want people to acquire information that is useful but potentially discouraging: diagnostic tests, genetic screens, financial-risk disclosures, performance feedback, and early-warning reports. This paper studies why such information may be avoided and how disclosure policies can be designed to increase voluntary take-up. A signal is evaluated together with the continuation environment that follows disclosure. The decision maker values the standard instrumental benefit of information, but also places weight on the worst posterior choice situation that the signal can generate. As a result, a more accurate signal can be rejected when it exposes a posterior with a sufficiently low continuation value. The analysis turns this diagnosis into a disclosure-design problem. Coarser information is the benchmark remedy: it increases take-up by limiting how bad the worst posterior realization can be. The paper then studies two complementary design responses. Downside support makes precise information acceptable by improving the consequences of bad news. Gradual release makes precise information acceptable by replacing one large disclosure decision with sequential voluntary choices evaluated at intermediate posteriors. A stylized medical-testing application illustrates how coarsening, protected disclosure, and staged follow-up can increase demand for diagnostic information. The results suggest that useful information is more likely to be adopted when designers protect individuals from unfavorable posterior consequences or sequence exposure to those consequences.

title: Net-Positive Management: A Governance, Risk, and Compliance Meta-Framework

detail.title: Net-Positive Management: A Governance, Risk, and Compliance Meta-Framework
detail.abstract: Organizations implementing multiple management-system standards face structural fragmentation: independent scopes, duplicated evidence, and parallel audit cycles that erode strategic coherence and degrade governance into checklist compliance. This whitepaper introduces Net-Positive Management (NPM), a governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) meta-framework that integrates existing standards without replacing them. NPM is organized by four structural commitments: a teleological criterion derived from Polman and Winston's Net Positive standard; a logical gate of five ethical invariants grounded in Ellul's ethics of self-limitation and Jonas's ethics of responsibility; a Domain-Driven Design architecture (Evans, Brandolini) that models governance over stakeholder impact surfaces rather than organizational hierarchies; and a dynamic causal analytics pipeline (DCCA) operating under Pearl's structural causal models and Gama's concept-drift adaptation. The framework produces a traceable chain from strategic purpose through Bounded Contexts, Ethical Performance Indicators (EPIs), and Behavioral Event Signals (BES) to audit evidence. NPM materializes in seven artifacts constituting a Minimum Viable Compliance baseline and eight phases orchestrating their production and continuous verification. The whitepaper formalizes the ethical gate, the MCDA weight architecture, the DCCA four-control loop, and the operationalization of invariant standards, including extraction limits and the reasonable-third-party test. The framework is standards-agnostic and jurisdiction-adaptable.

title: Proxy Optimization and Institutional Hollowing A Two-Stage Theory of Proxy Governance and Legitimacy Collapse
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Proxy Optimization and Institutional Hollowing A Two-Stage Theory of Proxy Governance and Legitimacy Collapse
detail.abstract: Institutional failures often appear sudden to outsiders while seeming long anticipated by insiders. This paper develops a two-stage theory of institutional failure to explain that divergence. The central mechanism is proxy optimization: the substitution of auditable indicators of performance, compliance, or legitimacy for the substantive standards those indicators were meant to approximate. In Stage One, proxy optimization produces internal hollowing: substantive judgment weakens, enforcement becomes selective, norm clarity declines, and internal actors adapt to measured compliance rather than substantive performance. External legitimacy remains buffered during this phase by reputation, procedural defensibility, and stakeholder inertia. In Stage Two, a triggering event makes the accumulated divergence between proxy performance and substantive degradation externally legible, producing a nonlinear collapse of trust and reactive restructuring. Building on Goodhart’s Law, Campbell’s Law, organizational decoupling, legitimacy theory, and audit culture, the paper argues that proxy optimization is locally stabilizing but globally corrosive. The model is illustrated through stylized credentialing and corporate examples and specifies conditions under which proxy-based governance is most likely to produce institutional fragility.

title: Mobile Trading Interfaces as Behavioral Decision-Support Filters: Sentiment Sensitivity, Design Rules, and Overtrading Risk

detail.title: Mobile Trading Interfaces as Behavioral Decision-Support Filters: Sentiment Sensitivity, Design Rules, and Overtrading Risk

declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because the empirical analysis uses stock-day level trading and sentiment data and does not involve human subjects, patient data, surveys, experiments with human participants, individual-level brokerage accounts, personally identifiable information, or private personal data. The analysis is conducted at an aggregate stock-day level and is used to study decision-support patterns in mobile trading interfaces.

detail.abstract: Mobile trading apps have made investing an always-on activity in which investors can react quickly to emotional signals embedded in public text. This study reframes that environment as a decision-support design problem: a mobile interface is not a neutral window to the market, but a behavioral filter that can either dampen or amplify sentiment-driven trading. We develop a design-facing framework that links practical interface levers, including notification pacing, light confirmation steps, and source prioritization, to changes in the marginal sensitivity of trading activity to sentiment. The framework also uses simulations to map where filtering is likely to help and where it may unintentionally backfire. Empirically, we analyze stock-day panel data from 2009 to 2013, an early utility-oriented phase of mobile trading. Sentiment is measured from two channels, curated financial news and user-generated blogs, and separated into positive and negative tone. The focal outcome is the marginal semi-elasticity of sentiment with respect to trading volume, which captures how strongly trading activity responds to small changes in sentiment. We compare this sensitivity before and after mobile interfaces become widely available and examine heterogeneity across exposure segments and macro market conditions. The results show a clear attenuation in the marginal sensitivity of trading volume to negative sentiment after mobile rollout. This pattern motivates channel-and segment-specific interface configurations that place more protection on noisier, user-generated negative signals while preserving access to more verifiable curated information. The findings translate into decision-ready guidance: filter more strongly where noise and mobile exposure are high, preserve access to higher-quality information, and consider adaptive interface modes that adjust to market conditions. The paper offers empirically testable design rules for mobile investing interfaces without relying on claims of perfect causality.

title: Evaluating 'Minilateralism' As A Deterrent: A Comparative Review of How Contemporary IR Literature Assesses the Efficacy of the Quad versus the BRICS/SCO in India's Strategy to Constrain China

detail.title: Evaluating 'Minilateralism' As A Deterrent: A Comparative Review of How Contemporary IR Literature Assesses the Efficacy of the Quad versus the BRICS/SCO in India's Strategy to Constrain China
detail.abstract: This literature review seeks to explore the academic discourse around the role of minilateralism and multilateralism as tools of asymmetric deterrence vis-à-vis China in the post-Galwan India (2020-ongoing). Rooted in theories surrounding minilateralism and soft balancing, the following study examines the dominant theme of India's increasing participation through Quad, in contrast to the alternative explanations of India's strategic engagement in organizations dominated by China, such as BRICS and SCO. The thesis presented here suggests that while the academic discourse has been successful in identifying India's institutional dynamics, there is a key empirical shortcoming that needs to be addressed. By integrating International Political Economy (IPE) frameworks, this paper questions whether India's use of institutional tactics serves as an effective deterrent, or whether it merely provides diplomatic cover to an expanding structural economic asymmetry and deepening trade dependency between the two states.

detail.abstract: Cloud computing was meant to simplify IT, yet scale and standardization have created operational complexity that raises the value of managed service intermediaries (MSPs). This paper explains when intermediation mainly redistributes value (profit migration) versus when it creates new value (pie expansion), and when coexistence between a cloud provider and an intermediary can be sustained rather than ending in disintermediation. We develop a parsimonious sequential model in which the provider sets wholesale terms and a direct offer, the intermediary chooses a resale offer and capability investment (e.g., optimization, integration, governance), and heterogeneous clients choose channels based on net value. The analysis yields two demand-and-profit regimes and two sustainability mechanisms: relationship/switching frictions can discipline bypassing, and wholesale over-extraction can backfire by weakening intermediary investment and shrinking demand, producing an interior coexistencesupporting fee and a role for alliance/sharing rules. In this market, the key competitive lever is not the retail fee but the provider's wholesale terms and the intermediary's capability investment, and only their interaction separates profit migration from pie expansion.

title: An Analytical Study of Louis Fry’s Spiritual Leadership Model from the Perspective of Quranic Teachings
affiliations: Qum Seminary and

detail.title: An Analytical Study of Louis Fry’s Spiritual Leadership Model from the Perspective of Quranic Teachings
detail.abstract: This study explores Louis Fry’s model of Spiritual Leadership and evaluates it through the lens of the teachings of the Holy Quran. The findings indicate that Fry’s model—with its emphasis on concepts such as vision, altruistic love, faith and hope, meaning and purpose, membership, and organizational commitment—can contribute to enhanced productivity, job satisfaction, and organizational cohesion. However, the analysis reveals that, in comparison to the comprehensive Quranic approach, Fry’s model does not fully encompass the divine and spiritual dimensions. The principles of spiritual leadership in the Holy Quran are rooted in monotheism (tawḥīd), human dignity, justice, and moral values, aiming ultimately at spiritual elevation and divine approval. Aligning Fry’s model with Quranic teachings demonstrates that, although it attends to employees’ spiritual needs, it requires revision and integration with Quranic principles to serve as a holistic and value-aligned managerial framework, particularly within Islamic organizations. This study employs the thematic exegetical method (istinṭāqī) developed by Martyr Ṣadr to examine the model’s compatibility with Quranic teachings. The study recommends revisiting contemporary leadership models, including Fry’s, in order to offer a God-centered vision, reinforce ethical and spiritual values, and deepen the ethos of service and justice—ultimately constructing a culturally grounded and more effective framework for organizational leadership. Based on the teachings of the Holy Quran, concepts such as divine vision, divine love and mercy, faith and trust in God, purposeful divine orientation, spiritual responsibility and membership, and divine commitment can be regarded as foundational elements of a conceptual model for spiritual leadership.

title: Attested Governance: Runtime Integrity for Autonomous Systems

detail.title: Attested Governance: Runtime Integrity for Autonomous Systems

The author is also the founder and sole owner of Attested Intelligence Holdings LLC (Illinois File No. 17233815), which holds prosecution rights to that application and develops the Attested Governance Artifacts (AGA) implementation referenced in the paper. The paper argues for an architectural category that admits multiple implementations beyond AGA, and Section 1.3 together with the Conflict of Interest Disclosure addresses the relationship between that general argument and this specific implementation.

detail.abstract:
Autonomous AI systems face four critical governance problems: attestation of subject identity and authorized behavior, runtime enforcement of policy, generation of cryptographically meaningful evidence, and continuity verification of decision history. These four problems are coupled by design: any architecture that solves them must address all four under one trust root. The case making them actively pressing now is the rise of autonomous AI agents that manage workflows, invoke external tools, and modify state at production scale without cryptographic records that survive forensic scrutiny. We name this property inseparability. The architecture either binds all four pillars under one cryptographic chain (integrated) or it does not (composed). This commitment is made at the time of design. Composing independent provenance, policy, attestation, and logging produces parallel verification with multiple independent trust roots. Integration requires the architectural commitment to a unified receipt format and trust model from system genesis. 
We define Attested Governance as the integrated category and present AGA as one implementation. The category supports multiple architectural realizations; Section 3.4 reviews peer instantiations. We derive the integration property within an explicit trust boundary that names two assumptions upfront: the issuing authority and the portal are not compromised. We present AGA in detail including its primitive choices, trust model design, and operational framing. We anchor the architectural pattern in three independent regulated sectors (industrial control under ISA/IEC 62443-3-3 and NIST SP 800-82, custody transfer measurement under API MPMS Chapter 21.1, and electronic records integrity under 21 CFR Part 11) where the same four-pillar pattern has operated for decades under high consequence requirements where evidence must survive external audit. A reference implementation establishes an empirical baseline: a complete signed measurement cycle completes in approximately 4.94 ms on commodity hardware (reference implementation, v0.9.1 snapshot; see Section 4.7), with post-quantum hybrid signing adding only 0.39 ms per governance decision (Hybrid Sign + Verify mean). We propose six minimum criteria for standardization within the category, identify four open research directions, and identify three IETF working groups (SCITT, RATS, WIMSE) as standardization pathways. 
The proposed category is motivated by high consequence contexts demanding forensic review. We do not claim it applies to all AI governance. The architectural debt of partial governance becomes more expensive to retire as autonomous systems scale into higher consequence deployments, and the same forensic scrutiny pressure that drove regulated sectors (Section 5) toward integration applies here. Whether a coherent category with interoperable implementations emerges depends on whether the integration question is engaged structurally now.

title: Digital Green Transformation: Policy Coordination Mitigates Energy Misallocation

detail.title: Digital Green Transformation: Policy Coordination Mitigates Energy Misallocation

keywords: New energy demonstration city pilot program

detail.abstract: Against the backdrop of an escalating global energy crisis, fully harnessing the synergistic effects of policy instruments is not only a practical imperative to alleviate current energy misallocation but also a critical pathway to enhancing energy efficiency. This study innovatively integrates the smart city pilot program (SCPP) and the new energy demonstration city pilot program (NEDCPP) into a unified analytical framework, drawing on panel data from Chinese A-share listed firms spanning 2007–2023. By applying the multi-period difference-in-differences with double machine learning (DID-DML) method, we systematically investigate the mitigating effect of digital–green policy synergy (DGPS) on corporate energy misallocation. Our key findings are as follows: (1) DGPS significantly reduces corporate energy misallocation relative to either policy implemented in isolation, exhibiting a robust "1 + 1 > 2" synergistic effect—results that withstand a battery of robustness checks and rigorous endogeneity treatments. (2) DGPS alleviates energy misallocation indirectly through three distinct channels: improving information transparency, optimizing factor allocation efficiency, and accelerating the integration of digital and green technologies. (3) The mitigation effect of DGPS is significantly stronger in old industrial base cities, low-competition industries, and mature firms. Collectively, these findings offer empirical support and actionable policy insights for authorities seeking to optimize policy portfolios and strengthen energy governance effectiveness.

title: Sanctions and Creative Trade: Evidence from Russia
affiliations: Bilecik University

detail.title: Sanctions and Creative Trade: Evidence from Russia
detail.abstract: This paper examines how sanctions affect Russia’s bilateral creative trade, focusing on the sanction episodes following the 2014 annexation of Crimea and the 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Using annual bilateral data for 197 countries over the period 2002–2023 and drawing on recent advances in gravity-based trade estimation, the analysis situates sanctions involving Russia within a general-equilibrium-consistent global trade framework. The results show that sanctions involving Russia are associated with large and persistent declines in Russia’s bilateral creative trade, with effects intensifying across successive sanction episodes. The magnitude of these effects varies substantially across partner countries and by sanction direction, suggesting notable heterogeneity in Russia’s creative trade responses to sanctions.

title: Improving Environmental Management of Agricultural Plastic Waste: Spatiotemporal Analysis of GHG Emission Factors and Policy-relevant Scenarios toward Carbon Neutrality in Japan
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Improving Environmental Management of Agricultural Plastic Waste: Spatiotemporal Analysis of GHG Emission Factors and Policy-relevant Scenarios toward Carbon Neutrality in Japan
detail.abstract: Designing effective environmental management strategies for plastic waste requires accurate and region-specific information on greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. However, existing national-average emission factors (EFs, kg-CO2/kg-waste plastics) fail to capture regional heterogeneity, potentially leading to biased policy decisions. This study analyzed region-specific EFs for Japan by integrating local waste quantities and regionally differentiated recycling practices. Additionally, future national trends of the EFs and waste quantities were estimated to assess changes in future GHG emissions through introducing improved recycling practices (e.g., increasing recycling ratios). The estimated regional EFs ranged from -1.98 to 1.21 (kg-CO2/ kg-waste plastics) and differed markedly from national values; in some regions, the sign of the EFs was even reversed, indicating that failing to consider regional differences in EFs can lead to flawed policymaking. The estimated future GHG emissions show that, although EFs for polyolefin (PO) and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) films decrease similarly with improved recycling practices, the resulting GHG reductions are greater for PO. This is because future PVC waste quantities are projected to approach zero, whereas those of PO decline only modestly; this demonstrates that for PO, decreasing not only its EFs but also its waste quantities is necessary to reduce more emissions. These results underscore the variation of GHG reduction depending on policy design and the importance of prioritizing advances in recycling practices for PO to achieve greater GHG reductions. Overall, the region-specific EFs developed in this study improve the accuracy of GHG estimation and provide an evidence-based foundation for more effective waste management and policymaking.

title: Settled Out Of Congress: Section 301 Settlement Agreements, the Agreements on Reciprocal Trade, and the Constitutional Limits of Trade Made Beside the Treaty
affiliations: New York Law School

detail.title: Settled Out Of Congress: Section 301 Settlement Agreements, the Agreements on Reciprocal Trade, and the Constitutional Limits of Trade Made Beside the Treaty
detail.abstract:
In February 2026, the Supreme Court held in Learning Resources, Inc v Trump, 146 S. Ct. 628 (2026), that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act does not authorize the President to impose tariffs. The decision closed one route to unilateral trade restructuring and, in the same paragraph, identified Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 as the constitutional model of a bounded tariff delegation. The Executive accepted the signal immediately.

This Article examines the instrument now being built on that foundation: the Agreement on Reciprocal Trade, concluded neither as an Article II treaty nor under Trade Promotion Authority, but as the settlement of a Section 301 investigation under 19 U.S.C. § 2411(c)(1)(D). It argues that these agreements occupy unmapped constitutional space that established doctrinal categories do not describe; that their legality turns on a scope question no court has yet resolved; and that their constitutional vulnerability, though real, is, by design, largely insulated from judicial correction.

Applying the Youngstown tripartite framework and Hathaway's durability hierarchy, the Article shows that Section 301 settlements tied to investigated conduct sit in Jackson's Category 1 (express congressional authorization), while settlements that restructure a partner's regulatory architecture across uninvestigated subjects drift toward the constitutional twilight zone. The major questions doctrine, correctly applied, reaches the scope of the settlement, not the existence of the delegation.

The Article identifies two realistic paths to judicial review and explains why the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA/CUSMA) is simultaneously the most consequential target of the Agreement on Reciprocal Trade strategy and the instrument through which it can most plausibly be contested under Section 303 of the Trade Act. The settlement route is strongest where it is narrowest. That paradox, not litigation, is its principal constraint.

title: Next 24 h Rockburst Probabilistic Warning Using Microseismic Monitoring and Machine Learning

detail.title: Next 24 h Rockburst Probabilistic Warning Using Microseismic Monitoring and Machine Learning
detail.abstract: Rockburst was considered a typical dynamic hazard during deep underground construction, with strong abruptness and time variability. To achieve short-term warning of rockburst occurrence time, this study proposed a next 24 h probabilistic warning method based on microseismic (MS) monitoring and machine learning. Two deep-buried tunnel projects were selected as the study objects. Based on field construction records, rockburst investigation results, and MS monitoring data, a case database containing 184 typical rockburst events was established. The number of MS events, energy, apparent stress, and apparent volume were selected as input features. Daily time-series samples were constructed using sliding time windows, and the warning of rockburst occurrence time was transformed into a binary probabilistic prediction problem of whether a rockburst would occur within the next 24 h. A BiLSTM-Transformer model was developed to extract short-term continuous variations and long-range temporal dependencies of MS activity. The results showed that the proposed model effectively identified rockburst risk within the next 24 h, with AUC and AP values of 0.995 and 0.962 on the test set, respectively. The 7 d input window provided a good balance among short-term disturbance response, risk accumulation representation, and warning stability. Typical cases showed that the predicted probability usually entered a high-risk warning state approximately 3 d before rockburst occurrence and further increased as the rockburst approached. The MS response before rockburst showed coordinated multi-parameter evolution rather than a continuous increase in a single parameter. Increased apparent stress reflected local stress adjustment, increased apparent volume indicated fracture scale expansion, and the simultaneous enhancement of energy, apparent stress, and apparent volume indicated concentrated energy release and rapid fracture development. Reliability analysis showed that the predicted probability was generally consistent with the observed rockburst frequency, providing a practical reference for short-term rockburst warning in deep tunnels.

detail.title: Circular Economy in Post-Crisis Recovery: Closed-Loop Models as a Tool for Regional Economic Sustainability

detail.abstract: The shift of economic systems towards circularity is perceived as a priority in terms of recovery from the crisis and ever more macroeconomic instability. Closed loop models are seen less as a tool of environmental reconstruction, but rather, a structural mechanism to enable economic modernisation and sustainability at large. Conversely, the quantitative estimation of the effects of circularity on broader-macroeconomic-dynamics are still meagre, especially in terms of a more comparative crosscountry dimension. Our purpose with this study is to focus on the development and testing an integrated Grid-locked technique to empirically estimate the impact of circularity on the economic sustainability of the European Union, in the crisis haven, "ad virum". Recovery path. The balanced panel comprises the EU-27 for 2015-2024 (270 country-year observations). The countries in the sample are heterogeneous in significant ways: the gap in real GDP per capita exceeds three times; the share of industry in GDP ranges from about 15-30%; the level of urbanization ranges from about 55% to more than 80%; circularity indicators show more than twofold crosscountry differentiation. Together, this warrants the use of a panel model with country and time fixed effects. Our methodology proceeds on the formation of composite indices of circularity and economic resilience based on minmax normalizing indicators across the whole panel of observations and then econometrically estimating them using a fixed effects model (Stata 17.95% confidence interval, clustered robust standard errors, Hausman test for specification selection). The circularity index combines resource productivity, recycled materials use, waste recycling, environmental expenditures and the share of renewable energy; the economic sustainability index combines real GDP per capita, employment stability and investment activity. The results show a statistically significant positive correlation between the integrated circularity index and the economic resilience index for the years 2021-2024 when controlling for structural characteristics of economies (industry structure, investment, urbanization) and for time invariant national characteristics. The growth of the integrated circularity index relates to an increase the aggregate index of economic sustainability in the post-crisis period. There is also a tendency to reduce the crosscountry variability of economic resilience in recovery phase. The significance of the study in practice is showing the feasibility of integrating circular indicators into the system of macroeconomic monitoring and strategies for longterm structural stabilization within the European Union.

detail.title: Mapping the Market for Ideas in Europe, 1450-1650: A Title-Embeddings Approach

keywords: O33 market access; monopolistic competition; spatial product differentiation; useful knowledge; Industrial Enlightenment; word embeddings; USTC; early modern Europe; print; knowledge diffusion

publicationDetails.detailsText: GMU Working Paper in Economics No. 26-26
publicationDetails.journalName: George Mason University Department of Economics Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Between 1450 and 1650 European print transformed from a Mainz craft producing about 3,000 Latin editions per decade into a market of nearly 800,000 editions across seven major languages and 1,300 cities. Did this expansion of the market for books and ideas change the way knowledge was organized and did that reorganization in turn shape city growth? Using title-level embeddings of the Universal Short Title Catalogue and a gravity-style city-period market access panel for six languages (Latin, German, Italian, French, Dutch, Spanish), we find that within-city increases in market access make a city's print output more topically diverse, less distinct from the European centroid, and more topically even. This pattern is consistent with monopolistic competition under spatial product differentiation rather than with Smithian specialization. The useful-knowledge share of this compositional response carries growthrelevant content beyond market access, predicting subsequent 50-year city population growth, consistent with Mokyr's Industrial Enlightenment thesis operating at the city level through trans-European scholarly print.

title: Thermal adaptation migration characteristics and thermal comfort evaluation modification of Chinese traditional dwellings: A case study on Pingyao Ancient City
affiliations: Tianjin Chengjian University, Tianjin Chengjian University, Tianjin Chengjian University, Tianjin Chengjian University, Tianjin Chengjian University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Hebei University of Engineering

detail.title: Thermal adaptation migration characteristics and thermal comfort evaluation modification of Chinese traditional dwellings: A case study on Pingyao Ancient City
detail.abstract: Due to the differences in regional climate, economy and culture, the current international thermal comfort standards are not applicable to all building types in China, especially traditional dwellings. In this paper, old-type traditional dwellings that have been preserved intact, improved-type dwellings that have undergone localized renovations, and new-type dwellings in the antique style in Pingyao Ancient City, Shanxi Province, China, were selected as case studies. Firstly, winter thermal comfort models were established for these dwellings using field measurements and questionnaires, while K-means clustering was employed to classify the existing building types. Secondly, regression analysis clarified occupants' thermal adaptation migration across environments. Thirdly, physiological acclimation was incorporated to modify the PPD model. Finally, introducing adaptive coefficient λ and expectancy factor e yielded modified aPMV and PMVe models. Results showed clustering further revealed distinct thermal stability and localized spatial variation among the three types. Notably, old-type dwellings remained non-neutral (11.1–12.3 ℃) throughout the heating season; however, this prolonged discomfort stimulated robust adaptation, yielding the lowest neutral (13.50 ℃), comfort (12.63 ℃), and preferred (14.31 ℃) temperatures. Conventional frameworks underestimated occupants' cold-climate adaptability, whereas our modified models closely matched empirical experiences. This research enriches the ASHRAE Global Thermal Comfort Database and references thermal comfort evaluation in cold-region vernacular architecture.

title: Tax Incentives, Artificial Intelligence, and Firm-Level Employment Growth: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Firms

detail.title: Tax Incentives, Artificial Intelligence, and Firm-Level Employment Growth: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Firms
detail.abstract: Using panel data on Chinese A-share listed firms from 2011 to 2022, this paper examines the impact of tax incentives on firm-level employment growth and the moderating role of artificial intelligence (AI). Based on a two-way fixed effects model, the results show that tax incentives significantly promote employment growth by improving after-tax cash flows and easing financing constraints. To address endogeneity concerns, an instrumental variable approach is employed using the industry–province–year average level of tax incentives, and the positive effect remains robust under two-stage least squares estimation. Further analysis reveals that higher levels of AI adoption significantly amplify the employment effects of tax incentives, indicating that digital technologies enhance the efficiency of fiscal policy transmission to labor demand. Heterogeneity analysis shows that these effects are more pronounced among non-state-owned firms and firms facing weaker audit constraints. This study provides micro-level evidence on the interaction between tax policy and digital transformation.

title: Optimal Food Basket for Older Adults in Six Regions of Argentina
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Optimal Food Basket for Older Adults in Six Regions of Argentina
detail.abstract: Introduction: The United Nations has designated 2020-2030 as the Decade of Healthy Aging, highlighting the need for policies that promote quality of life among older adults. Nutrition plays a central role in this process. How ever, before designing adequate nutritional policies, it is essential to de ne an optimal diet and assess its feasibility given real-world constraints. Ob jectives: This study aims to determine optimal diets for Argentina's elderly population, regionally adapted, nutritionally adequate, and a ordable under the minimum retirement pension. Study design: Using data from Argentina's 2017-2018 National Household Expenditure Survey, food consumption and prices in six regions were analyzed. Main outcome measures: Nutritional and cost data were processed using linear and non-linear programming in GAMS software to construct three models: (1) minimizing cost subject to nutri tional requirements; (2) adding food group variability constraints; and (3) minimizing deviation from observed consumption while meeting nutritional and budget constraints. Results: Cost-minimization alone yields unrealis tic diets nutritionally adequate but lacking variety and cultural acceptabil ity. Including food group constraints improves balance but results in low palatability. The third model, which respects observed consumption pat terns, produces diverse and culturally relevant diets that meet nutritional and budgetary goals. Conclusion: Diets aligned with local habits and pref erences, rather than strictly cost-based formulations, are more feasible and sustainable for older adults. These ndings underscore the importance of combining nutrition science with behavioral, cultural, and economic factors when designing public food policies for aging populations.

title: A Computationally Efficient Two-Dimensional Finite Element Model for Climate-Driven Soil–Pipe Interaction in Buried Pipelines
affiliations: University of Warwick, University of Birmingham, University of Birmingham, University of Birmingham, University of Birmingham and University of Birmingham

detail.title: A Computationally Efficient Two-Dimensional Finite Element Model for Climate-Driven Soil–Pipe Interaction in Buried Pipelines
detail.abstract: Buried pipelines are critical components of UK infrastructure, but they are increasingly exposed to climate-driven soil movement, often resulting in differential settlement. There is therefore a need for computationally efficient tools to support large-scale risk assessment of buried pipelines under changing ground conditions. This study investigated whether a two-dimensional (2D) modelling approach can reproduce the key soil–pipe interaction behaviour predicted by a calibrated three-dimensional (3D) model under varying soil moisture conditions. A parametric analysis was carried out in PLAXIS 3D, which served as the high-fidelity reference model for the soil–structure interaction. The 3D model was first calibrated against experimental data for a concrete pipe and then used in a parametric study in which the water content within an active zone above and around the pipe was varied between 26% and 32%. In parallel, a two-dimensional (2D) finite element model (FEM) was developed in Python and can produce results within seconds. Comparative analysis indicates that the simplified model reproduces the displacement trends and magnitudes obtained from PLAXIS 3D simulations while reducing the computational cost by two orders of magnitude, highlighting its potential for large-scale climate resilience assessment of buried pipeline networks.

title: Multi-source error-aware post-refinement for reliable multi-distress segmentation in intelligent pavement inspection
affiliations: Southwest Jiaotong University, Southwest Jiaotong University, Southwest Jiaotong University and Southwest Jiaotong University

detail.title: Multi-source error-aware post-refinement for reliable multi-distress segmentation in intelligent pavement inspection
detail.abstract: Reliable multi-distress segmentation is essential for intelligent pavement inspection, yet single-stage segmentors often produce coarse predictions with missed regions, fragmented structures, and boundary ambiguities under complex roadway conditions. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multi-source error-aware segmentation corrector (MESC), a backbone-adaptable post-refinement framework for improving unreliable coarse predictions without modifying pretrained baseline architectures. The proposed MESC jointly exploits image-domain evidence and logit-domain priors through a dual-stream cross-domain fusion network (DS-CDFN), where a bidirectional cross-attention unit (BCAU) is introduced to promote multi-scale feature interaction between structural details and semantic confidence cues. A weighted composite objective is further used to guide error-focused correction while suppressing over-correction in reliable regions. Comprehensive evaluations on a private multi-distress dataset and two public crack benchmarks, Crack500 and Yang Crack Dataset (YCD), demonstrate consistent improvements across heterogeneous baselines. On the private dataset, MESC improves mean F1-score (mF1-score) and mean intersection over union (mIOU) by 2.50%~7.06% and 4.24%~10.91%, respectively. On Crack500 and YCD, F1-score gains reach 0.67%~1.50% and 0.51%~9.39%, with corresponding IOU gains of 0.86%~1.87% and 0.81%~13.37%. Moreover, trustworthiness analysis demonstrates that MESC enhances prediction reliability, and latency evaluation further shows that it introduces a relatively stable overhead of 7~11 milliseconds (ms). These indicate that MESC can improve segmentation accuracy and prediction reliability while maintaining manageable deployment overhead, highlighting its promising potential for intelligent pavement inspection.

title: A Time–Frequency Synergistic Graph Neural Network for Wind Power Forecasting
affiliations: Quanzhou University of Information Engineering, Tianjin Conservatory of Music, Quanzhou University of Information Engineering, University of Information Engineering, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Tianjin Conservatory of Music and Quanzhou University of Information Engineering

detail.title: A Time–Frequency Synergistic Graph Neural Network for Wind Power Forecasting
detail.abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting is critical for grid stability and energy management, yet existing methods often struggle with modeling multivariate dependencies, capturing complex temporal structures, and optimizing hyperparameters. This paper proposes a Time–Frequency Synergistic Graph Neural Network (TFGraphSTN) that integrates three complementary branches: a time-domain branch (CorrPatchNet) with Multivariate Correlation Attention (MVCA) to dynamically capture inter-variable dependencies; a frequency-domain branch employing a differentiable Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) and frequency-domain attention to extract multi-scale spectral features; and an Adaptive Frequency-domain Graph Convolution (AdaptiveFreqGCN) branch that propagates frequency-specific information over an adaptive adjacency matrix to model spatial correlations among turbines. The outputs are fused via learnable weighted summation and a gating mechanism for end-to-end forecasting. Experiments on the SDWPF dataset demonstrate that TFGraphSTN achieves a validation composite score of 38.43, substantially outperforming the state-of-the-art MLAGCN (43.44) under their respective evaluation settings. Ablation studies reveal that each branch contributes independently, with the frequency-domain branch providing the largest gain (Score increase of 1.95 upon removal). On an independent test set, the model attains a Score of 43.87, confirming its competitive generalization capability. This work offers a new paradigm for multivariate time series forecasting by seamlessly unifying time–frequency analysis with graph neural networks.

title: Cross-border carbon pricing, industrial energy use and export competitiveness: Evidence from China’s Plastics and articles thereof exports to the EU
